  "abstract_verbatim": "For every fixed $`1\\le q\\le4`$, critical square-lattice random-cluster Dobrushin interfaces converge to chordal $`\\mathop{\\mathrm{SLE}}\\nolimits _{\\kappa(q)}`$, where $`\\kappa(q)=4\\pi/\\arccos(-\\sqrt q/2)`$, and the complete nested plane loop collections converge to whole-plane $`\\mathop{\\mathrm{CLE}}\\nolimits _{\\kappa(q)}`$. The results hold under uniform marked Jordan boundary approximation and retain loop multiplicities and traversals. <a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> For every fixed $`1\le q\le4`$, critical square-lattice random-cluster Dobrushin interfaces converge to chordal $`\mathop{\mathrm{SLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}`$, where $`\kappa(q)=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)`$, and the complete nested plane loop collections converge to whole-plane $`\mathop{\mathrm{CLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}`$. The results hold under uniform marked Jordan boundary approximation and retain loop multiplicities and traversals. At <i>q</i> = 1 we obtain Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges.

- **claim-interfaces-nested-loops** (theorem, [source](#stmt-intro-main)): For every fixed real $1\le q\le4$, the following assertions hold.* 1. *For every bounded Jordan domain $D$ with distinct boundary marks $a,b$, and every approximation satisfying <a href="#intro:marked-jordan" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:marked-jordan">[intro:marked-jordan]</a>, the Dobrushin strand $\eta_n$ converges in law, in <a href="#intro:curve-metric" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:curve-metric">[intro:curve-metric]</a>, to chordal $\operatorname{SLE}_{\kappa(q)}$ from $a$ to $b$ in $D$.* 2. *Under the specified free infinite-volume law, $\Gamma_\delta$ converges in law as $\delta\downarrow0$ to the nested whole-plane $\operatorname{CLE}_{\kappa(q)}$, in the spherical collection topology just defined. The limit is Möbius invariant.* *Both conclusions hold along every mesh sequence. No uniformity in $q$ is asserted.
  - Explanation: Identifies the separate interface and complete nested loop scaling limits for each fixed critical parameter, retaining curve order and collection multiplicity.
- **claim-cardy-bond-crossings** (theorem, [source](#stmt-intro-cardy)): Let $\psi:D\to\mathbb H$ send $a,c,d$ to $0,1,\infty$, and put $x=\psi(b)\in(0,1)$. Under the boundary and approximation conventions above, $$\label{intro:cardy-formula} \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P(C_n) =\frac{\displaystyle\int_0^x[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,\mathrm dt} {\displaystyle\int_0^1[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,\mathrm dt}.$$
  - Explanation: Determines the limiting probability of an actual bond crossing with the prescribed free boundary convention.
- **claim-positive-loop-law** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-loop-law)): On a genus-zero tile surface with positive cap completions, the switch weight $d^\ell$, where $\ell$ counts completed medial loops, is proportional to the critical FK weight with the corresponding boundary partition. Conditional laws on common subdomains are therefore FK laws with induced partitions. The same assertion holds after interchanging the colors. On a torus without caps the two weights differ by a factor bounded in terms of $q$ alone.
  - Explanation: Relates completed-loop weights to critical random-cluster weights and identifies induced conditional laws.
- **claim-finite-plane-loops** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-finite-loops)): For every $1\le q\le4$, all medial strands of the specified free infinite-volume square FK law are almost surely finite loops. Finite deterministic surgeries admit positive normalized loop laws with the FK conditional laws of Lemma <a href="#prelim:loop-law" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:loop-law">3</a>.
  - Explanation: Excludes infinite medial strands and permits normalized laws after finite deterministic surgeries.
- **claim-collar-density-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-prelim-collar)): Suppose two positive laws have the same graph in a collar between radii $r$ and $16r$. In this collar the graph is a full annulus, or a bounded number of sectors separated by straight coordinate walls; coincident slit banks are allowed. Their deterministic wire portions agree there. Only boundedly many wire blocks traverse the collar, and no other identifications jump it. One radial side faces an arbitrary unknown partition, whereas the graph and deterministic wires toward the other side are fixed. The marginal densities on edges beyond that other side are mutually bounded by a constant independent of scale and of the far graph. Equivalently, their expectations of every nonnegative remote function are comparable with this same constant.* *The conclusion also holds for a fixed-shape rectangular bulk collar shielding a long box, with a constant depending on its shape.
  - Explanation: Bounds remote marginal density ratios through the specified common collar without dependence on its scale or the far graph.
- **claim-relative-collar-contraction** (bound, [source](#stmt-prelim-relative-collar)): Under the hypotheses of Lemma <a href="#prelim:collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:collar">5</a>, suppose successive collars have one of the following geometries:* 1. *a full annulus, or one sector whose through wires are precisely continuous primal wire portions along its side rays;* 2. *two sectors, with primal wires along both side rays of one sector and no through wires in the other, and no further fixed contacts between the sectors.* *After $m$ further collars of a sufficiently large fixed radius ratio, the remote expectations of every fixed nonnegative function under two possible unknown-side laws have ratio $1+O((1-c)^m)$, or both expectations vanish. The conclusion holds in either radial direction, also after positive modifications or tilts supported on the unknown side.
  - Explanation: Contracts the relative influence of unknown boundary data across successive admissible collars, including positive unknown-side tilts.
- **claim-exponential-passage-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-prelim-passages)): In any fixed buffered annulus or sector of the preceding types, a raw passage count $X$ satisfies $$\label{prelim:passage-moment} \mathbb E[\exp(BX)\mid\text{exterior}]\le C_B \qquad(0\le B<\infty),$$ uniformly in scale and in exterior states inducing the specified graph and arbitrary boundary partition. The same holds for a fixed finite family of macroscopic passage counts in a fixed geometry.
  - Explanation: Controls passage counts at every fixed exponential rate under the specified conditional positive laws.
- **claim-local-tilt-stability** (bound, [source](#stmt-prelim-tilts)): For fixed $b>0$, put $$F_j=\mathbb E b^{N_j},\qquad d\nu_j=F_j^{-1}b^{N_j}\,d\mathbb P.$$ The ratios $F_j/F_{j-1}$ are bounded above and below uniformly. Under $\nu_j$, the shell counts $X_i$ at and beyond the outer tilt level, $i\ge j$, have all fixed exponential moments uniformly bounded. The assertions remain conditional on exterior data of the specified geometry and allow adjoining a fixed family of passage counts with buffers at or beyond that level.
  - Explanation: Bounds successive nest-weight normalizations and preserves exterior shell exponential moments under the local tilt.
- **claim-absorb-passage-errors** (bound, [source](#stmt-prelim-absorb)): Suppose $Y_n\ge0$, $\mathbb E Y_n\ge n^{-A}/C$, and $\mathbb E Y_n^2\le Cn^A$, whereas $X_n\ge0$ has uniformly bounded exponential moments at every fixed rate. For fixed $C_0\ge1$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, $$C_\varepsilon^{-1}n^{-\varepsilon} \le \frac{\mathbb E[Y_n C_0^{\pm X_n}]}{\mathbb E Y_n} \le C_\varepsilon n^{\varepsilon}.$$
  - Explanation: Absorbs exponential passage factors at arbitrarily small polynomial cost when the positive observable has the stated moment bounds.
- **claim-separated-slit-partitions** (bound, [source](#stmt-prelim-surface)): Let finitely many straight finite wall segments have fixed macroscopic shapes and positive mutual separation. Complete each as a positive isolated boundary slit. Let $Z_s$ be its partition function relative to the unmodified plane law, and $Z_{\rm all}$ the corresponding partition function with all slits. Uniformly in the mesh, $$\label{prelim:surface-factorization} Z_{\rm all}\asymp\prod_s Z_s.$$ Reversing every cap-wire polarity on both banks of a straight isolated segment with boundedly many changes alters $Z_s$ by a bounded factor. The same comparison holds for a segment and its image, with transported cap data, under a symmetry of the homogeneous tile lattice, with the two color names exchanged when the symmetry exchanges the color lattices.
  - Explanation: Compares the combined slit partition with the product of isolated slit partitions and controls the specified polarity and symmetry changes.
- **claim-local-cost-stability** (bound, [source](#stmt-exp-local-costs)): Changing a cutoff radius by a fixed factor, changing the fixed compatible exterior completion, applying a tile-lattice symmetry to the experiment, or interchanging both color names and wire designations changes each of these logarithms by $O(1)$. The expectations of the local weights, their fixed powers, and the same arm indicator have logarithms of size $O(\log n)$. For some $c>0$, $$\label{exp:strict-arm} P(n)\le-c\log n+O(1).$$
  - Explanation: Controls local logarithmic costs under fixed convention changes and proves strict decay of the actual arm probability.
- **claim-logarithmic-budgets** (bound, [source](#stmt-exp-comparisons)): With the definitions above, $$\begin{aligned} 2P+2D_*+4(C_0+C_1)&\le o(\log n),\label{exp:rectangle-budget}\\ C_0+C_1+L_0+L_1&\le o(\log n),\label{exp:corner-budget}\\ P+\sum_j\log\frac{F_-(a_j)}{F_+(a_j)} &\le o(\log n),\label{exp:charge-budget} \end{aligned}$$ where the finite list of fixed charges in the last inequality satisfies <a href="#exp:charge-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="exp:charge-range">[exp:charge-range]</a> and $\sum_j a_j=1$.
  - Explanation: Bounds the combined flat-change, corner and bulk-charge logarithmic costs without requiring limiting critical exponents.
- **claim-local-cap-elimination** (construction, [source](#stmt-exp-cap-elimination)): For disk arcs whose boundary intervals contain at most one wire flip, their positive cap-loop factors are $d$ for a zero-flip high starting port and $1$ for a zero-flip low starting port or a one-flip arc, up to a bounded overall loop-count error and an error $d^{O(X)}$ for remaining macroscopic arcs. A nest of $N$ straddling arcs at a corner of turn $g\pi$ without a wire flip has negative-expansion weight relative to its caps comparable to $f(g)^{N/2}$.
  - Explanation: Evaluates local cap-loop factors and the relative corner-nest weights, leaving controlled macroscopic passage errors.
- **claim-balanced-polygon-budget** (construction, [source](#stmt-exp-polygon-budget)): Let a fixed simple rectilinear polygon have $m$ concave and $m+4$ convex true corners, with wire changes in side interiors. It has tile approximants differing by $O(1)$ mesh units such that at least $\lfloor m/2\rfloor$ corners of each relative wire type occur in each of the convex and concave sets, also after global wire reversal. For these approximants, $$\label{exp:polygon-saving} 3P+D_*+\sum_{v\,\mathrm{convex}}C_{i(v)} +\sum_{v\,\mathrm{concave}}L_{i(v)} \le\frac12P-\frac32D_*+o(\log n).$$ Each fixed family of negative endpoint charges with magnitudes summing to one has total wrong-to-correct local logarithmic cost at most $-P+o(\log n)$.
  - Explanation: Chooses balanced corner parities and combines the local inequalities into a strict polygon budget.
- **claim-angular-transfer-decay** (bound, [source](#stmt-bulk-angular-estimate)): Fix a compact interval $I\subset(-v,v)$. Let $B_{\rm in}$ be a product of $P_\zeta$ rows and $B_{\rm out}$ a product of $P_\xi$ rows, at real angles in $[-v,v]$. Suppose each product contains at least $n\ge1$ angles in $I$. Uniformly for $x,y\in[-v,v]$, $$\begin{aligned} \\|B_{\rm out}N(x)B_{\rm in}\\|&\le Cn^{-1+\rho}, \label{bulk:low-estimate}\\ \\|B_{\rm out}\{N(x)-e^{i\tau(x-y)}N(y)\}B_{\rm in}\\| &\le Cn^{-1-\rho}.\label{bulk:high-estimate} \end{aligned}$$ The constant depends on $q$ and $I$. Boundedly many additional pairs of before-twist rows may be inserted immediately to the right of $N$, and additional pairs of after-twist rows immediately to its left. The two terms in <a href="#bulk:high-estimate" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="bulk:high-estimate">[bulk:high-estimate]</a> may use different such insertions; on each side their counts must be even. The constant may depend on a bound for these counts. Multiplication of $D$ by a common scalar multiplies the bounds by its absolute value.* *The same estimates hold in the physical square array sliced in a diagonal time direction: its time angles are $\pm\gamma_0$, where $\gamma_0=\pi/4$, and its space angles alternate between $\pi-\gamma_0$ and $\gamma_0$. The exterior states may contain any finite number of physical row and spin insertions outside the sandwich. A scalar contraction is bounded by the displayed rate times the two reflection norms, with the squares centered on a cut included in its reflection kernel.
  - Explanation: Suppresses the low insertion and its high angular difference between strict-row sandwiches, with physical contractions controlled by exterior reflection norms.
- **claim-plane-row-hilbert-space** (construction, [source](#stmt-bulk-plane-kernels)): Finite words of homogeneous normalized strict-angle rows have limiting Gram matrices as $N\to\infty$. Their quotient and completion give a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ with unit vector $\Omega$ and bounded left row actions satisfying $$\label{bulk:row-bound} \\|A^D(\alpha)\\|\le2\\|D\\|.$$ Bare vacuum coefficients are continuous in strict angles and are unchanged by a common translation of all time angles, as long as the translated angles remain in $(-v,v)$.
  - Explanation: Constructs a separable Hilbert space from limiting row Gram matrices with bounded row actions and common-angle translation invariance.
- **claim-self-adjoint-angle-generator** (construction, [source](#stmt-bulk-boost)): There is a self-adjoint operator $B$ on $\mathcal H$ such that $V_th=e^{tB}h$ locally for each word $h$. Ordinary strict-angle words form a graph core for $B$. Each family $A^D$ extends to a bounded holomorphic operator function on $\|\operatorname{Re}z\|<v$, with $$\label{bulk:imaginary-covariance} A^D(x+ib)=U_bA^D(x)U_{-b},\qquad U_b=e^{ibB}.$$
  - Explanation: Realizes angle translation through a self-adjoint generator and obtains bounded holomorphic row families with imaginary covariance.
- **claim-scalar-fixed-band-continuation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-bulk-edge-band)): Almost every spectral function $f$ extends analytically and without zeros to bands of one fixed positive width about the lines $\operatorname{Re}z=\pm v$. It has modulus one on those lines and satisfies $\|f(z)\|\le1$ in the intervening strip. At any specified point of the strip, the set of spectral functions vanishing there has measure zero.
  - Explanation: Continues almost every spectral function through common boundary bands, proves zero-freeness there and controls its strip modulus.
- **claim-current-isotopy-invariance** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cur-deformation)): In the positive winding expansion, the primitive is invariant, pairing by pairing, under simple-path isotopies that continue its initial lift, keep its endpoints in their regions, and avoid the other insertions. The statement is a tensor identity for arbitrary outside spins. A pure diagonal string obeys the corresponding deformation rule without a source.
  - Explanation: Preserves the current primitive under admissible path isotopies as an identity for arbitrary outside spins.
- **claim-current-tree-evaluation** (construction, [source](#stmt-cur-tree-weights)): For an arc $e:i\to j$ bounding its child interval, put $m=h_i-h_j$ and $$\label{cur:weights} \begin{aligned} w_e&=\frac{\cos((m-\tfrac12)\lambda)}{\sin\lambda},& k_e&=-\frac{\cos((m+\tfrac12)\lambda)}{\sin\lambda},\\ a_e&=e^{-i\lambda(h_i+h_j)},& c_*&=\frac{e^{-i\lambda}}{2\sin\lambda}. \end{aligned}$$ For each fixed pairing, the primitive to $z$ is the sum over a marked edge of the separator-tree path from $p$ to the region of $z$: use $k_e$ on earlier edges, $c_*a_e$ on the marked edge, and $w_e$ on every other boundary arc. Unmarked internal loops have weight $d$, and a marked closed loop contributes zero.* *For a pure $K(Q)$ string to $z$, use $k_e$ on the full separator-tree path and $w_e$ off it. An internal loop enclosing $z$ then has weight $-2$ instead of $d$. The parity of the number of such loops records the color change from the boundary-tree region to the lattice color of $z$.
  - Explanation: Evaluates primitives and pure strings through separator-tree edge weights and the enclosing-loop parity rule.
- **claim-clear-slab-extraction** (bound, [source](#stmt-cur-slab-estimate)): Suppose a diagonal-time slab of macroscopic thickness about a low or high stencil contains no other non-diagonal tensors or endpoints. Diagonal chains may cross the slab. The stencil has an intact neighborhood disjoint from all other chains except its own prefix, and the slab has spare margins for routing and cuts. Bounded lattice errors are permitted inside these margins. Then the stencil contraction can be written as the corresponding low or high expression in Theorem <a href="#bulk:angular-estimate" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="bulk:angular-estimate">15</a>, between exterior states independent of the choice of stencil term. Only boundedly many compensating pairs of rows and a common bounded scalar are introduced.* *In particular, if the two clear parts of the slab contain at least $n$ physical steps, its scalar contraction is bounded by $Cn^{-1+\rho}$ for a low stencil, and by $Cn^{-1-\rho}$ for a high stencil, times the two exterior reflection norms. Reflected stencils satisfy the same statement.
  - Explanation: Expresses a local stencil as an angular sandwich with common exterior states, retaining their reflection norms in the bound.
- **claim-boundary-tree-normalization** (construction, [source](#stmt-four-tree)): The number of loops closed by the local boundary caps is $$\mathcal I=\#\{\text{unwired tree vertices}\}. \label{four:loop-count}$$ Exactly one of $E_{\mathfrak A},E_{\mathfrak B}$ occurs. Completing the four open ports around $A,C$ adds respectively one and two loops on these events.* *For an edge $e$ represented by an arc $i\to j$, $i<j$, put $$m_e=h_i-h_j,\qquad w_e=\frac{\cos((m_e-\tfrac12)\lambda)}{\sin\lambda},\qquad k_e=-\frac{\cos((m_e+\tfrac12)\lambda)}{\sin\lambda},\qquad a_e=x^{h_i+h_j}. \label{four:edge-weights}$$ Let $\mathcal P(V)$ be the root-to-$V$ edge path. Define $$\begin{aligned} D_V&=d^{-\mathcal I}\prod_{e\in\mathcal P(V)}k_e \prod_{e\notin\mathcal P(V)}w_e,\label{four:D}\\ H_V&=d^{-\mathcal I}\sum_{e\in\mathcal P(V)}a_e \prod_{f\text{ before }e\text{ in }\mathcal P(V)}k_f \prod_{f\text{ not before }e,\ f\ne e}w_f. \label{four:H} \end{aligned}$$ Thus $H_{\rm root}=0$. If $e$ joins its parent $u$ to its child $v$, the common product $D_e^\circ$, with the factor on $e$ omitted, satisfies $$H_v-H_u=a_eD_e^\circ,\qquad D_u=w_eD_e^\circ,\qquad D_v=k_eD_e^\circ. \label{four:recursion}$$
  - Explanation: Counts cap-closed loops by unwired tree vertices, identifies the exclusive actual-connection alternatives and supplies observable recursions.
- **claim-corrected-boundary-observable** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-marked)): Call the tree *typical* when all four terminal legs have positive length. On a typical tree, $$D_p=D_b=D_{d_0}=0,\qquad \frac{H_b}{P_0G}=\begin{cases}1&E_{\mathfrak A},\\d&E_{\mathfrak B},\end{cases} \quad \frac{H_{d_0}}{P_0G}=y\begin{cases}d&E_{\mathfrak A},\\1&E_{\mathfrak B}. \end{cases} \label{four:marked-values}$$ On the gap visits of any interval $R$, $$\begin{gathered} \Re(H_V/A_R)-c_R(\operatorname{col}(V))D_V \quad\text{is constant},\\ c_R(\text{wire color})=-\cos\lambda,\qquad c_R(\text{other color})=\cos(2\lambda). \end{gathered} \label{four:line-invariant}$$ Set $$\Gamma(\mathfrak A)=P_0y^2,\qquad \Gamma(\mathfrak B)=-P_0y,\qquad H_V^\circ=H_V-\Gamma(\operatorname{col}(V))D_V. \label{four:corrected}$$ The variables $H_V^\circ$ are bounded uniformly over all trees and vertices. On a typical tree they have value $P_0GT$ along the $c$-leg and all its descendant branches, where $$T=\mathbf1_{E_{\mathfrak A}}+y\mathbf1_{E_{\mathfrak B}}. \label{four:T}$$ On gap visits along $B$, their only possible values are $H_b,P_0GT$; along $C$, they are $H_{d_0},P_0GT$.
  - Explanation: Computes marked values and boundary line invariants and makes the corrected observable uniformly bounded across all tree shapes.
- **claim-observable-compactness-shielding** (bound, [source](#stmt-four-compactness)): For every fixed positive power, the moments of $\|H_{V(z)}\|+\|D_{V(z)}\|$ are bounded by a power of $\min(1,\|z-c\|)^{-1}$, uniformly when $z$ is farther than a mesh-scale distance from $c$. The expectations in <a href="#four:observable" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="four:observable">[four:observable]</a> are asymptotically equicontinuous on interior compact sets. Every lattice parity therefore has the same locally continuous subsequential limits.* *Typicality has probability tending to one. As a macroscopic interior point approaches an ordinary boundary point, including a polygon corner, its tree vertex visits that point’s interval with probability tending to one after the mesh limit. Near $b,c,d_0$ it lies beyond an edge of the corresponding terminal leg with high probability; near $p$ an unpassed $L=3$ edge remains with high probability.
  - Explanation: Provides moment bounds and interior equicontinuity, then shields ordinary boundary points and the marked terminal legs.
- **claim-diagonal-boundary-residual** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-residual)): For every bounded function $\gamma$ of the two colors and every boundary point $u$ distinct from the four marks, $$\lim_{z\to u}\limsup_{n\to\infty} \left\|\mathbb E_{\rm open} [\gamma(\operatorname{col}(V(z)))D_{V(z)}]\right\|=0. \label{four:boundary-residual}$$ Here $z$ in the outer limit is a macroscopic interior location, and any lattice vertices tending to it may be used in the inner limit.
  - Explanation: Cancels the color-weighted diagonal residual in the mesh limit followed by an ordinary boundary approach.
- **claim-conditional-conformal-identification** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-four-conditional-map)): Suppose an interior subsequential limit $h$ of $h_n$ is holomorphic in the ordinary complex coordinate, and pass simultaneously to a limit $r$ of $P_{\mathfrak A}$. Then $0<r<1$. Put $$U_0=r+d(1-r),\qquad V_0=dr+1-r,\qquad T_0=r+y(1-r). \label{four:target-vertices}$$ The function $h$ maps $\Omega$ conformally onto the interior of the simple polygon with successive vertices $0,U_0,T_0,yV_0$, taking $p,b,c,d_0$ to those vertices. If a conformal half-plane coordinate takes the marks to $0,\chi,1,\infty$, respectively, then $$r=\frac{\displaystyle\int_1^\infty u^{\rho-1}\|u-\chi\|^{\rho-1}\|u-1\|^{1-3\rho}\,du} {\displaystyle\int_\chi^\infty u^{\rho-1}\|u-\chi\|^{\rho-1}\|u-1\|^{1-3\rho}\,du}. \label{four:crossing-formula}$$ Under deterministic separate $\mathfrak A$ caps the corresponding crossing probability is $r/(r+d(1-r))$.
  - Explanation: Identifies a holomorphic subsequential observable with the target polygon map and derives distinct open-cap and deterministic-cap crossing probabilities.
- **claim-positive-distant-normalization** (bound, [source](#stmt-wall-distant)): For sufficiently large fixed $L$, under the exterior positive tilt $\nu_U\propto U\mu$, $$\mathbb E_{\nu_U}(Y/U)\ge c_L>0,\qquad \mathbb E_{\nu_U}\|Y/U\|^p\le C_{p,L} \label{wall:distant-moments}$$ for every fixed $p>0$, uniformly for large $R_0$ and fine mesh.
  - Explanation: Bounds the distant normalization away from zero and controls its moments under the exterior positive tilt.
- **claim-complete-wall-factorization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-wall-factorization)): For the complete wall, there are probe-independent complex numbers $a_n(R_0,L)$, bounded above and away from zero in modulus for the fixed large $L$, such that $$\mathcal H_{\rm full}(z,u) =a_n(R_0,L)h_n(z)J_n(u)+o(1) \label{wall:factorization-eq}$$ uniformly on interior compact probe sets. The error tends to zero with mesh first and then $R_0\to\infty$. No limit of $a_n$ is asserted or needed.
  - Explanation: Factors the complete-wall observable into interior and exterior factors with a nonvanishing probe-independent coefficient in the stated limit order.
- **claim-positive-gap-closure** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gap-closure)): Keep the distant charges and their locations fixed. Let $g$ denote the gapped wall and $f$ the wall obtained by closing the specified $h$-gaps, retaining any other gaps and tip factors. There are positive probe-independent numbers $b_n$, bounded above and below, such that $$\mathcal H_g(z,u)=b_n\mathcal H_f(z,u)+o(1) \label{gap:comparison}$$ uniformly on interior compact probe sets. The error vanishes in the mesh limit followed by $h\to0$. Constants may depend on the fixed remaining features. In particular, a second, smaller collection of gaps may be closed before the first collection.
  - Explanation: Closes the selected wall gaps through a positive bounded scalar comparison after the mesh limit.
- **claim-finite-reflection-templates** (construction, [source](#stmt-hol-templates)): For fixed primary gap widths and every $\varepsilon>0$, one can choose finitely many reflection and extraction steps and finitely many secondary gaps so that the expected extracted count of each original marker is at least $1-\varepsilon$. The cuts have strict macroscopic clearances. On any compact set of eligible probe pairs, finitely many such templates suffice, and one may use the union of their secondary gaps. All choices precede the mesh limit.
  - Explanation: Constructs finite reflection and extraction templates with strict clearances and arbitrarily small expected marker deficit.
- **claim-mixed-derivative-saving** (bound, [source](#stmt-hol-mixed-bound)): For fixed primary gaps and sufficiently small fixed secondary gaps chosen as in Lemma <a href="#hol:templates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="hol:templates">30</a>, there is $c>0$ such that $$\left\| (\delta_{1,z}^{(2)}+i\delta_{2,z}^{(2)}) \delta_{j,u}^{(2)}\mathcal H_g(z,u)\right\| =O(n^{-2-c}) \label{hol:mixed-decay}$$ uniformly on the eligible compact probe sets. The constants and reflection-tree size may depend on these fixed gaps.
  - Explanation: Combines angular extraction and positive feature savings into strict mixed derivative decay at fixed gaps.
- **claim-holomorphic-disk-limit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-hol-disk)): For every rational orthogonal polygon with the four flat marks and balanced approximations specified above, every locally continuous subsequential limit of $h_n$ is holomorphic. Consequently the boundary identification and crossing formula of Proposition <a href="#four:conditional-map" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:conditional-map">26</a> hold without its holomorphicity premise for these polygons.
  - Explanation: Discharges the holomorphicity premise of the boundary calculation for the prescribed balanced rational polygons.
- **claim-jordan-crossing-transfer** (theorem, [source](#stmt-jordan-transfer)): Consider the marked, uniformly convergent square lattice polygon approximations $(D_n;a_n,b_n,c_n,d_n)$ to a bounded Jordan quadrilateral $(D;a,b,c,d)$ in the four-mark sense of Subsection <a href="#intro:crossings" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:crossings">1.3</a>. Keep every edge of the polygon graph random, and separately wire the two closed arcs $a_nb_n$ and $c_nd_n$, with no other primal identifications. If $\psi:D\to\mathbb H$ sends $(a,c,d)$ to $(0,1,\infty)$ and $\chi=\psi(b)$, the probability of an actual open path between these arcs tends to $g(\chi)$.
  - Explanation: Transfers actual crossing probabilities to marked Jordan quadrilaterals while keeping all graph edges random and the electrodes separately wired.
- **claim-free-bond-cardy-specialization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-jordan-cardy)): At $q=1$, with every edge, including every boundary edge, sampled independently with probability $1/2$ and with no wiring, the probability of the event $C_n$ defined in Subsection <a href="#intro:crossings" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:crossings">1.3</a> tends to $$\frac{\displaystyle\int_0^\chi [t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,dt} {\displaystyle\int_0^1 [t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,dt}.$$
  - Explanation: Specializes the actual-path comparison to independent bond percolation with free boundary edges.
- **claim-compatible-simple-interface-drawing** (construction, [source](#stmt-moving-drawing)): The prescribed polygon graph and its Dobrushin strand admit a tile and collar representation in a Jordan polygon $V_n$ such that:* 1. *$V_n$ has the same marked uniform Jordan limit as $D_n$;* 2. *the rounded strand is simple, visits the same ordered local pieces as the prescribed medial strand, and is at curve distance $O(\delta_n)$ from it;* 3. *at every switch-revealing stop, the remaining domain is a simple slit disk. Under deterministic cap closure its unrevealed edges have the original conditional FK law, with known open edges contracted and known closed edges deleted;* 4. *primal and dual banks of the prefix have physical access to their corresponding known edges and wire vertices within $O(\delta_n)$. Every completion of the unknown edges embeds its actual paths in the slit disk without crossing the past.* *The construction can use identical domains and caps away from an interval where two additional boundary changes are inserted.
  - Explanation: Constructs a nearby simple tile drawing that preserves the original conditional law, ordered local visits and physical bank accesses.
- **claim-small-interval-asymptotics** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moving-asymptotic)): For $f$ in <a href="#jordan:functions" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="jordan:functions">[jordan:functions]</a>, $$f(1-\chi)=1-f(\chi),\qquad f(\chi)=c_q\chi^h(1+o(1))\quad(\chi\downarrow0), \qquad c_q>0.$$
  - Explanation: Establishes the crossing function's complementary symmetry and positive leading small-interval asymptotic.
- **claim-moving-four-change-test** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moving-slit)): Let a four-change strand in $V_n$ be stopped before completing its strand, revealing only the switches it has encountered. Let $U_n$ be its remaining simple slit disk, with the tip as the new starting mark. Consider histories for which a fixed basepoint has a fixed positive disk in $U_n$, and the four prime-end marks in a disk chart normalized at that basepoint remain mutually separated by a fixed positive amount. Then, on these histories, $$\label{moving:limit} \mathbb P_{\mathrm{open}}(E_{\mathrm P}\mid\mathcal F_n) -f(\chi_{U_n})\ \longrightarrow\ 0 \quad\hbox{in probability}.$$ Here $E_{\mathrm P}$ is the primal pairing event, equivalently the actual bridge event after separate primal closure, and $\chi_{U_n}$ is its current ordered cross-ratio. The assertion holds for arbitrary mesh-dependent stopping rules satisfying this localization.
  - Explanation: Identifies conditional pairing probabilities in localized explored domains in probability over histories.
- **claim-chart-oscillation-modulus** (bound, [source](#stmt-moving-chart-modulus)): Let $u_n$ be the horizontal coordinate of the conformal rectangle map of $U_n$, with the designated primal arcs at $0$ and $1$. Under the localization in Theorem <a href="#moving:slit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="moving:slit">37</a>, there is a common modulus tending to zero for the oscillation of $u_n$ on a connected path of vanishing physical diameter, including paths with accesses to the prime boundary. Consequently, for $\beta>0$, a possible primal path starting in $\beta\le u_n\le1-\beta$ cannot reach a known primal-open edge or a primal electrode inside a sufficiently small physical ball. “Possible” means that all still unknown primal edges are filled open, before any external wire jump is permitted.
  - Explanation: Controls chart oscillation along physically small connected paths and excludes short central-band accesses to known primal attachments.
- **claim-protected-edge-deletion** (bound, [source](#stmt-moving-deletion)): Fix a history and use separate deterministic primal closure. Deleting a set of still random edges changes the actual crossing probability by at most the conditional probability that an endpoint of a deleted edge reaches a wire interval by an actual open path, allowing one initial test step over the deleted edge. For a central-band set contained in a ball of radius $r$, this cost is bounded by a quantity tending to zero as $r\downarrow0$, uniformly in the history and center, provided its required outer radius is fixed and the mesh is sufficiently small. The same holds for any fixed finite number of such balls.
  - Explanation: Bounds deletion effects by actual electrode attachment and makes protected central-ball costs vanish uniformly under localization.
- **claim-flagged-cell-six-arm-cost** (bound, [source](#stmt-moving-flags)): In a fixed bulk block let $\pi$ be a simple known primal bank path. Choose fixed scales $\ell\ll R_1$, away from its endpoints and the original boundary. Flag a deterministic grid cell of side $\ell$ if, in its annulus from $100\ell$ to $R_1$, the prefix already supplies four cyclically alternating actual arms, its two primal arms being known wired bank paths. If a candidate within $O(\ell)$ of this cell actually connects to an electrode, then six actual alternating arms occur in a cropped annulus from $200\ell$ to $R_1/2$. For a bounded region covered by the deterministic cells, the averaged conditional attachment cost of all flagged cells is at most $$\label{moving:flag-sum} C\ell^{-2}(\ell/R_1)^{2+c_0}=O_{R_1}(\ell^{c_0}).$$ The statement remains valid with one initial test step and with the bounded cap changes in <a href="#moving:odds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="moving:odds">[moving:odds]</a>.
  - Explanation: Turns attachments near flagged history cells into actual alternating arms and bounds their averaged conditional cost.
- **claim-directed-obstacle-comparison** (construction, [source](#stmt-moving-obstacle)): After removing histories of arbitrarily small probability and allowing an arbitrarily small conditional deletion cost, there is a Jordan polygon $H$ containing the basepoint, selected from a finite list at each fixed accuracy, with the following properties. Its boundary follows the original boundary and explored prefix to that accuracy; away from finitely many protected balls and flagged cells it has fixed positive clearance from all central candidates. As the accuracies decrease, $H$ and $U_n$ have the same pointed kernel limits. Artificial marks in $H$ may be chosen with disk angles arbitrarily close to the corresponding angles in $U_n$.
  - Explanation: Builds finite-list Jordan obstacles with candidate clearance, controlled deletion cost and matching pointed kernels.
- **claim-bounded-chordal-tests** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-tests)): For every $x>2R+1$, put $$\label{chordal:martingale} M_t(x)=\left(\frac{xg_t'(x)}{g_t(x)-W_t}\right)^h.$$ These processes and their reciprocals are bounded on the stopped range, uniformly in the mesh. For arbitrary stopping rules $0\le\sigma_n\le\tau_n$ in that range and uniformly bounded $\mathcal F_{\sigma_n}$-measurable tests $F_n$, $$\label{chordal:approx-martingale} \mathbb E\!\left[F_n\bigl(M_{\tau_n}(x)-M_{\sigma_n}(x)\bigr)\right] \longrightarrow0$$ under the original single-strand Dobrushin law.
  - Explanation: Obtains bounded approximate martingale tests under the original Dobrushin law without magnifying the shrinking-interval coupling error.
- **claim-brownian-driving-limit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-driver)): On every compact capacity interval, the Dobrushin driving functions converge in law, uniformly, to $\sqrt\kappa B_t$, where $B$ is standard Brownian motion and $$\label{chordal:kappa} \kappa=\frac{8}{1+h} =\frac{4\pi}{\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)}.$$
  - Explanation: Identifies the full compact-capacity driving limit through the drift and bracket fixed by the martingale tests.
- **claim-territorial-arm-counting** (bound, [source](#stmt-chordal-territories)): In a buffered bulk annulus, $m$ disjoint radial medial sublegs force at least $m$ alternating actual primal/dual arms in a further cropped annulus. If only one color is retained, one obtains at least one crossing in a distinct intervening strip per two assignments of that color to successive medial separators.
  - Explanation: Converts disjoint medial sublegs into alternating actual lattice arms with buffered cropping.
- **claim-physical-curve-tightness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-compactness)): The physical Dobrushin strands are tight in the uniform Euclidean curve topology modulo increasing reparametrization. Every subsequential limit has no nonconstant interval on the original boundary, and no interior point is visited three times with nonconstant excursions between consecutive visits.
  - Explanation: Proves uniform-curve tightness and excludes varying boundary intervals and genuine interior triple visits.
- **claim-avoidable-annular-traversals** (bound, [source](#stmt-chordal-avoidability)): At a switch-revealing stop of the Dobrushin exploration, call a component of $U_n\cap A(z;r,R)$ *avoidable* if it does not separate the tip access from the target access inside $U_n$. The conditional probability of a future radial traversal in any avoidable component is bounded by a quantity tending to zero as $r/R\downarrow0$, uniformly over histories and centers, with $r,R$ fixed before the mesh limit and $\delta_n\ll r$.
  - Explanation: Controls future traversal of avoidable components uniformly at actual revealing stops using a missing-color bank arm.
- **claim-target-cap-no-return** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-target)): After the strand first enters a shrinking initial conformal cap around its target, the probability of a subsequent displacement of fixed positive physical size tends to zero.
  - Explanation: Makes macroscopic return after entrance into a shrinking target cap negligible.
- **claim-dense-interior-double-visits** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-dense-doubles)): For ordinary chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$, $4<\kappa<8$, almost surely every nonempty open capacity interval contains both visits to some interior self-double point.
  - Explanation: Ensures interior self-double visits occur within every open capacity interval in the stated non-simple SLE range.
- **claim-small-gates-exclude-excursions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-gates)): In a joint subsequential limit of the physical strand and its Loewner driving function, the physical curve cannot enter an open component of a Loewner hull that is disjoint from the Loewner trace and the original boundary.
  - Explanation: Excludes physical excursions into swallowed open hull components by a first-gate stopping argument.
- **claim-ordered-chordal-convergence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-trace)): For every bounded marked Jordan domain and every marked uniform polygon approximation satisfying Equation <a href="#intro:marked-jordan" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:marked-jordan">[intro:marked-jordan]</a> with the boundary conventions of Subsection <a href="#intro:model" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:model">1.1</a>, the Dobrushin strand converges in law, in the uniform Euclidean oriented-curve topology modulo increasing reparametrization, to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_{\kappa(q)}$.
  - Explanation: Identifies the entire oriented curve, including possible capacity plateaus and the target tail, with chordal SLE in the strict parameter range.
- **claim-exact-pocket-factorization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-peel-factorization)): Conditionally on any finite exploration history, the unqueried switches in its remaining components have the positive cap laws described by their boundaries. Distinct components are conditionally independent. Before two targets split into distinct components their explorations are identical. A strand between successive pocket switches is a portion of one original closed loop.
  - Explanation: Factors unexplored components conditionally and preserves the shared exploration before target separation.
- **claim-chart-wall-crossings** (bound, [source](#stmt-peel-wall-rsw)): Fix a buffered corridor of bounded aspect in a normalized disk chart. Its terminal wall intervals lie strictly inside designated homogeneous arcs; one terminal interval may instead be an interior bar. After the mesh limit at this fixed scale, an actual crossing of either prescribed color $X$ has conditional probability bounded below, uniformly in the exploration history and its boundary partitions. At an $X$-wall it reaches an actual wall vertex. At an opposite-color wall it reaches the $X$-corner of an inward wall triangle. In the latter case a segment inside that triangle, ending at the midpoint of its base, completes the crossing to a screen and meets an actual $X$-path only at its starting corner.* *The two-sided bounded-density collar comparison of Section <a href="#sec:preliminaries" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:preliminaries">2</a> holds for such buffered chart collars on a homogeneous wall, with a bounded number of through-wire blocks.
  - Explanation: Obtains actual wall-reaching crossings and screening paths in fixed buffered charts with the precise triangle endpoint convention.
- **claim-reference-generation-tightness** (bound, [source](#stmt-peel-passages)): The number of edge-disjoint actual monochromatic cycles surrounding a fixed macroscopic ball in the initial square, and using no deterministic initial wall edge, is tight as the mesh tends to zero. Along finitely many target branches with bounded radial horizons, the number of reference-wall generations defined below is jointly tight.
  - Explanation: Bounds reference-wall generations through disjoint actual cycle counts on bounded radial horizons.
- **claim-peeled-domain-martingales** (theorem, [source](#stmt-peel-martingales)): For $x>0$ beyond these localization bounds, the quantities $$\label{peel:test} M_t(x)=\left(\frac{xg_t'(x)}{g_t(x)-W_t^{\mathbb H}}\right)^h$$ satisfy the approximate martingale identities between arbitrary causal stops on the segment. Tests may include the entire earlier exploration history of finitely many targets. The errors tend to zero after the mesh limit. The assertion concerns the averaged identities for this history law, not a uniform assertion over all deterministic mazes.
  - Explanation: Extends localized chordal test identities to peeled domains with the entire causal multi-target history retained.
- **claim-interior-radial-characteristics** (theorem, [source](#stmt-tree-interior)): Away from $\theta\in\{0,2\pi\}$, every limiting branch has the local characteristics $$\label{tree:sde} \begin{aligned} dW_t&=\sqrt\kappa\,dB_t+ \frac{6-\kappa}{2}\cot(\theta_t/2)\,dt,\\ dO_t&=\cot(\theta_t/2)\,dt,\qquad \theta_t=O_t-W_t. \end{aligned}$$ Here $t$ is that branch’s radial clock; the martingale identities hold relative to the full causal exploration history.
  - Explanation: Identifies radial driving characteristics away from forcepoint coincidence relative to the full causal history.
- **claim-coincidence-motion-barrier** (bound, [source](#stmt-tree-bar)): There are positive constants $c,C$ with the following property. Start at a causal stop with $\theta<r/16$, where $r>0$ is small. For $0<u\ll r^2$, the probability that $W$ advances counterclockwise by $r$ within additional radial time $u$, while $\theta<r/16$ until that advance, is at most $$\label{tree:bar-bound} C\exp(-cr/\sqrt u)+o(1).$$ The error vanishes in the mesh limit for fixed $r,u$. The constants in the limiting estimate are uniform in these parameters. Near $2\pi$ reverse the direction of motion and exchange the colors.
  - Explanation: Controls fast directed motion near coincidence through actual transverse bars and the prescribed restart direction.
- **claim-instantaneous-angular-reflection** (theorem, [source](#stmt-tree-reflection)): In its own radial clock, the limiting gap is the unique instantaneous reflected diffusion on $[0,2\pi]$ with interior generator $$\label{tree:generator} \mathcal A f(\theta)=\frac\kappa2 f''(\theta) +\frac{\kappa-4}{2}\cot(\theta/2)f'(\theta).$$ The forcepoint has no singular push: $$\label{tree:no-push} O_t=O_0+\int_0^t\cot(\theta_s/2)\,ds.$$ Equation <a href="#tree:sde" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:sde">[tree:sde]</a> consequently holds globally, including collisions, with locally integrable drift.
  - Explanation: Determines the unique reflected angular law and excludes a singular forcepoint push at endpoint times.
- **claim-joint-target-tree** (theorem, [source](#stmt-tree-joint-law)): For every finite family of deterministic interior targets, the peeling converges in its joint radial driving data to the target-invariant branching radial $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa(\kappa-6)$ tree. Branches agree until their target kernels separate and then have independent continuation noises. At successive full turns the force side is reversed, equivalently the angular gap remains instantaneously reflected on $[0,2\pi]$.
  - Explanation: Identifies the joint target-invariant radial tree with common branches before kernel separation and independent continuation noises afterwards.
- **claim-positive-loop-geometry** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-geometry)): The closed loop collections in the fixed square are tight for matching uniform curves modulo reparametrization and orientation. Constant limit curves may be removed. Their positive-diameter subsequential limits have the following properties almost surely.* 1. *Each deterministic interior point lies on no loop. Its absolute winding number about any loop is $0$ or $1$, and is stable along a converging loop sequence.* 2. *No interior point has three distinct visits in total among the loop elements. Visits include multiple traversals after constant pauses are removed and also multiplicity of different elements.* 3. *At every interior point of a positive loop, every neighborhood contains open disks of both absolute winding statuses for that loop.
  - Explanation: Establishes matching tightness, deterministic-point avoidance, stable winding and the total-visit and status-disk properties.
- **claim-default-loop-continuation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-continuation)): At an interior-angle time $s\in(a_k,b_k)$, the remaining traversal of $\widetilde L_z^k$ is the default strand from $W_s$ to $O_s$ in the current domain. In a chart sending those accesses to $0,\infty$, every finite portion of this continuation is ordinary chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ and is recorded by branches to targets from $\mathcal Z$ that remain accessible high above that portion. Every open nonconstant traversal interval of $\widetilde L_z^k$ contains two visits to one square-interior point.
  - Explanation: Realizes finite default continuations through accessible target branches and obtains double visits in every varying loop interval.
- **claim-discrete-winding-episode-order** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-episode-order)): As long as the target is macroscopically separated from a consumed tile or star, an episode is successful exactly when its terminal switch changes wall polarity. These polarity changes enumerate all loops surrounding the target, in their order from outside inward. A positive loop with positive clearance from the target is reached before a finite radial horizon depending on that clearance. Conversely a successful switch by a bounded horizon has macroscopic clearance from the target.
  - Explanation: Matches successful episodes to polarity changes and orders all surrounding loops with radial-horizon control.
- **claim-no-skipped-endpoint-resets** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-no-skip)): At a bounded-clock completed state with $\theta$ approaching $0$, the probability of returning to a fixed positive angle before a primal-pocket reset tends to zero, with the mesh limit first and the endpoint tolerance second. The analogous assertion near $2\pi$ uses a dual-pocket reset. Consequently the true successive discrete polarity-change times $b_k^n$ converge in probability to $b_k$ on sufficiently large finite horizons.* *Moreover, in an episode that succeeds by a bounded horizon, after a fixed interior-angle advance the probability of retreating arbitrarily near its starting endpoint before its successful switch tends to zero in the same order of limits.
  - Explanation: Prevents endpoint approaches from masquerading as resets and controls retreat within successful episodes in the stated limit order.
- **claim-canonical-ordered-containment** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-ordered)): For each $z\in\mathcal Z$ and $k\ge1$, the entire traversal of $\widetilde L_z^k$ occurs in cyclic order in $L_z^k$, possibly with extra traversal portions inserted. Its order occupies at most one turn of $L_z^k$. If two canonical labels give the same element, their lattice-limit labels give the same collection element.
  - Explanation: Embeds each canonical traversal in cyclic order within its lattice-limit element and preserves equality of canonical labels.
- **claim-bidirectional-label-equivalence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-label-equivalence)): Almost surely, simultaneously for all $z,w\in\mathcal Z$ and $k,j\ge1$, $$\label{loop:label-iff} L_z^k=L_w^j \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \widetilde L_z^k=\widetilde L_w^j$$ as collection elements.
  - Explanation: Proves equality of collection elements is equivalent for lattice-limit and canonical labels.
- **claim-loop-trace-traversal-identification** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-identification)): Every positive lattice-limit loop with an interior point has a canonical label. Matched elements have the same winding indicators on $\mathcal Z$. If either matched element stays away from the square wall, the two elements are equal as curves modulo reparametrization and orientation. Without that restriction, every canonical element is still contained in order in its lattice-limit partner.
  - Explanation: Labels every positive loop with an interior point and identifies matched curves when either element stays away from the square wall.
- **claim-critical-nested-plane-limit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-plane)): For every fixed $1\le q<4$, the loop collection of the free infinite-volume critical square-lattice FK law converges, through the full mesh sequence, to the nested whole-plane $\mathrm{CLE}_{\kappa(q)}$ in the spherical loop-matching topology of Subsection <a href="#intro:collections" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:collections">1.2</a>. The limit is Möbius invariant and includes every nested generation.
  - Explanation: Proves full-sequence nested whole-plane convergence for the critical free law in the strict parameter range, including spherical tails.
- **claim-endpoint-isometry-correlations** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-rr-rotation)): For every even $k\ge2$ and every compact $K\subset\mathcal D_k$, $$\lim_{\delta\downarrow0} \sup_{\boldsymbol u\in K}\sup_{I\in\operatorname{Isom}(\mathbb R^2)} \left\|\Phi_{k,\delta}(\boldsymbol u) -\Phi_{k,\delta}(I\boldsymbol u)\right\|=0. \label{eq:rr-target}$$
  - Explanation: Obtains uniform isometry invariance of even fair-signed height correlations on compact endpoint configurations.
- **claim-endpoint-six-vertex-correspondence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-rr-bkw)): After the fixed similarity identifying the medial square grid with $\mathbb Z^2$, the fair unit-jump height of critical plane $\operatorname{FK}_4$ has the same gradient law as the zero-slope six-vertex height with $\mathbf a=\mathbf b=1$ and $\mathbf c=2$.
  - Explanation: Identifies the plane fair unit-jump height gradient law with the specified zero-slope six-vertex law after the fixed similarity.
- **claim-endpoint-loop-count-escape** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rr-estimates)): Let $N(a,M)$ be the number of loops of diameter at least $a$ meeting $B(0,M)$. For $\delta$ sufficiently smaller than $a$, and every fixed $p<\infty$, $$\\|N(a,M)\\|_{L^p}\le C_p(1+M/a)^2. \label{eq:rr-count}$$ There are $C,\gamma>0$ such that, with harmless fixed changes of the radii, $$\begin{aligned} \mathbb P\{\exists L:L\cap B(0,M)\ne\varnothing, L\not\subset B(0,R)\} &\le C(M/R)^\gamma, && R\ge10M, \label{eq:rr-escape}\\ \mathbb P\{\exists L:\mathop{\mathrm{diam}}L\ge a, \mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(z,L)\le r\} &\le C\bigl((r+C\delta)/a\bigr)^\gamma, &&0<r<a/100. \label{eq:rr-point} \end{aligned}$$ The constants are independent of the deterministic center $z$.
  - Explanation: Controls macroscopic loop counts, escape and deterministic-point near-hits using bulk estimates.
- **claim-multiplicity-preserving-nail-coupling** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-rr-nails)): Fix $\alpha\in(0,\pi)$. As the mesh tends to zero, the construction of (Duminil-Copin, Kozlowski, Krachun, et al. 2026, sec. 3.6) [[DCKKMO2026Rotation](#ref-DCKKMO2026Rotation)] gives a coupling of two auxiliary loop samples. Their restrictions to a deterministic window exhausting the plane have, unconditionally, the respective homogeneous laws on $\delta\mathbb L(\pi/2)$ and $\delta\mathbb L(\alpha)$.* *Outside an event of probability tending to zero, there are correspondingly indexed, pairwise disjoint marked clusters, called nails, whose mesh tends to zero and whose window exhausts the plane. Corresponding nails have diameter tending to zero and lie at distance tending to zero from the same grid point. There is a bijection $\psi$ between all loops surrounding at least two but not all nails in the two samples. It preserves their oriented reduced crossing words relative to the nail grid.
  - Explanation: Extracts a bijection of non-trivial loops preserving oriented reduced crossing words, beyond a loop-set proximity statement.
- **claim-endpoint-whole-plane-field** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-rr-gff-input)): The fair unit-jump plane height of critical square-lattice $\operatorname{FK}_4$ converges on neutral smooth compactly supported tests to $\sqrt{2/\pi}$ times the whole-plane GFF with Green kernel $G(x,y)=-(2\pi)^{-1}\log\|x-y\|$. In particular, Proposition <a href="#q4field:wholeplane-input" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4field:wholeplane-input">73</a> holds.
  - Explanation: Applies the verified endpoint gradient and symmetry inputs to obtain the neutral-test whole-plane Gaussian field limit.
- **claim-height-convention-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4field-height-comparison)): Couple the cellwise lattice height $h_\delta^{\mathrm{cell}}$ and the height $h_\delta^{\mathrm{geom}}$ defined by the smoothed loop interiors using the same independent loop signs. For every smooth compactly supported neutral density $\rho$, $$\label{q4field:height-comparison-L2} \mathbb E\left\| \langle h_\delta^{\mathrm{geom}} -h_\delta^{\mathrm{cell}},\rho\rangle\right\|^2 \longrightarrow0.$$ This conclusion uses only bulk crossing and passage-count estimates.
  - Explanation: Shows that the geometric and cellwise height conventions agree asymptotically on neutral smooth tests in mean square.
- **claim-plane-height-characteristic-limit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4field-wholeplane-input)): For every real $\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb C)$ with $\int\rho=0$, the independent fair unit-jump height of critical square-lattice $\operatorname{FK}_4$ satisfies $$\label{q4field:plane-characteristic} \lim_{\delta\downarrow0} \mathbb E\exp\bigl(i\langle h_\delta,\rho\rangle\bigr) =\exp\left\{-\frac{\sigma^2}{2} \iint\rho(x)G_{\mathbb C}(x,y)\rho(y)\,dx\,dy\right\}.$$ The same assertion holds jointly for finitely many such tests.
  - Explanation: States the whole-plane characteristic-function limit and its joint neutral-test version with the prescribed normalization.
- **claim-neutral-height-moment-convergence** (bound, [source](#stmt-q4field-neutral-moments)): For finitely many smooth compactly supported neutral densities, their height pairings have uniformly bounded moments of every fixed order. All their joint moments converge to the corresponding Gaussian moments. The bounds and limits are unchanged by the $O(\delta)$ drawing modifications just described.
  - Explanation: Supplies uniform integrability at every fixed order and convergence of joint moments, stable under the specified drawing changes.
- **claim-binary-network-reflection-positivity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4field-reflection)): The plane binary-index network is reflection positive across the translated lattice symmetry lines parallel to either axis or to a diagonal. Reflection reverses directed transport and takes inserted matrices to their adjoints. Simultaneous conjugation by $SU(2)$ is unitary on the reflected Hilbert space.
  - Explanation: Establishes axial and diagonal reflection positivity, adjoint transport and unitary simultaneous conjugation.
- **claim-endpoint-bulk-four-arm-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-q4field-four-arm)): There is a constant $C$ such that, for $0<r<R$, $$\label{q4field:four-arm-bound} \limsup_{\delta\downarrow0}\pi_4^\delta(r,R) \le C(r/R)^2.$$ The same bound, with a constant depending on the fixed bulk collar, holds inside a domain with arbitrary exterior boundary data.
  - Explanation: Bounds the limiting bulk alternating-arm probability quadratically and transfers the estimate through fixed bulk collars.
- **claim-zero-dimensional-interior-contacts** (bound, [source](#stmt-q4field-contact-dimension)): In any tight subsequential limit of actual loops or Dobrushin strands, the interior set of genuinely distinct visits by macroscopic curves has Hausdorff dimension at most zero, almost surely. Constant parametrization pauses are discarded. No assertion about boundary contacts is made here.
  - Explanation: Bounds the interior macroscopic multiple-visit set after discarding constant pauses, without asserting a boundary-contact bound.
- **claim-vacuum-conditioned-wall-law** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4field-wall-law)): Conditioning the plane vacuum on exactly the stated wall switches gives the FK law inside with the indicated actual connections. For a closed $C$-wall, the $C'$ model on the strictly internal sites and its internal edges has free boundary condition. In a mixed wall, fixing the binary index at one transition port fixes the index of the distinguished strand; this condition has probability $1/2$ conditional on every switch configuration.
  - Explanation: Identifies finite-domain laws from actual wall constraints and the configuration-independent marked-index conditioning probability.
- **claim-free-bank-passage-arm-estimates** (bound, [source](#stmt-q4field-free-bank)): Consider a patch in which the bank color $C'$ has no forced open edge and no boundary identification on any domain wall meeting the patch. The graph may omit sites or edges. Counts of disjoint medial passages between buffered annular rims have moments of every order, uniformly in the mesh and in the remaining exterior data. The probability of an actual $C'$ arm across a ratio $R/r$ is at most $C_0(r/R)^\beta$ for some $\beta>0$. These statements hold as well for a product of free $C'$ models on disjoint subgraphs. In a bulk patch either color may be used.
  - Explanation: Controls passages and arms when the selected bank color has no local forced edges or wall identifications, allowing missing subgraphs.
- **claim-height-moment-kernel-compactness** (bound, [source](#stmt-q4field-moment-kernels)): For the regular polygons just specified, the height moment kernels at distinct interior points $z_1,\ldots,z_m$ satisfy $$\label{q4field:log-kernel} \left\|\mathbb E\prod_{i=1}^m h_\delta(z_i)\right\| \le C_m\bigl(1+\|\log(d_*\vee\delta)\|\bigr)^m, \qquad d_*=1\wedge\min_{i<j}\|z_i-z_j\|,$$ with $d_*=1$ when $m=1$. Here $C_m$ depends on $V$ and $m$, uniformly over the interior tuples, including those approaching the boundary. Geometric majorants for the conditional signed expansions have higher polynomial moments with corresponding logarithmic bounds. Integrated moments are uniformly integrable; the height laws are tight as local distributions, and their moment kernels are asymptotically equicontinuous on compact sets of distinct interior tuples. The count bounds hold also for arbitrarily shaped homogeneous walls in a fixed bounded box and for products of disks of one wall color.
  - Explanation: Controls logarithmic moment singularities, distributional tightness and off-diagonal equicontinuity for the prescribed wall experiments.
- **claim-regular-domain-dirichlet-field** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4field-regular-domain)): Let $V$ be a fixed polygon and let its actual wall approximations be as above. Then $$\label{q4field:Q} h_\delta\ \Longrightarrow\ u+\sigma\Phi_V \qquad\text{as distributions in }V,$$ where $u=0$ for a homogeneous wall and $u$ is the harmonic extension of the boundary values $0,1$ for a mixed wall. All joint integrated moments converge. At every tuple of distinct fixed interior positions, the moment kernels converge to those of the same field.
  - Explanation: Derives finite-domain Gaussian field convergence with the correct harmonic boundary term and integrated and pointwise moment conclusions.
- **claim-analytic-slab-displacement** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4field-analytic-displacement)): Consider two groups of vacuum insertions supported in finitely many pairwise separated rectangles, with a vacant projection slab between the two groups. Its normal is parallel to a lattice axis or a diagonal. Normalize each wall constraint by the probability of its isolated switch constraints; allow bounded charge and index factors. Translate one whole group farther across the slab. Every subsequential continuum correlation is real analytic in the translation distance on a neighborhood of $[0,\infty)$. This assertion also holds with other, previously fixed translations.
  - Explanation: Makes limiting normalized correlations analytic under rigid separation across a vacant admissible slab.
- **claim-local-neutral-factor-removal** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4field-neutral-removal)): Let finitely many cells of one finite rectangular grid, separated by positive-width grid gaps, contain normalized wall factors, bounded index factors, and charge factors. Let one cell contain only $$X_\delta(f)=\exp\bigl(i\langle h_\delta,-\Delta f\rangle\bigr), \qquad f\in C_c^\infty(\text{cell};\mathbb R).$$ In the expectation of the product, this factor may be replaced with error $o(1)$ by $$\label{q4field:neutral-mean} \mu(f)=\exp\left(-\frac{\sigma^2}{2} \int\|\nabla f\|^2\right).$$ The geometry and all gaps are fixed before $\delta\downarrow0$.
  - Explanation: Removes an isolated local Laplacian characteristic factor through reflection and analytic displacement at fixed geometry.
- **claim-endpoint-wall-gap-closure** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4field-close-gaps)): For fixed interior charge supports and, when present, a marked port, the local normalized charge laws with gapped and complete walls become arbitrarily close as follows: first take the mesh limit at fixed positive gap widths, and then let those widths tend to zero.
  - Explanation: Transfers local normalized charge laws from gapped to complete walls with the mesh limit taken before gap removal.
- **claim-exterior-readable-discrete-pockets** (construction, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-discrete-pockets)): In a homogeneous $C$-wall disk, each outer contour is the external perimeter of an outermost actual $C'$-cluster. Behind it lie pockets bounded by the maximal simple $C'$-open cycles, ordered by inclusion of their interiors. Their interiors are disjoint; several pockets can belong to one outer contour. The contours, these cycles, their assignment to contours, and all switches outside the pocket interiors can be determined without querying strictly interior switches. Conditional on these data, the pocket interiors have independent homogeneous $C'$-wall laws.* *In a two-arc disk, first reveal the distinguished path. On either side, its bank together with that side’s wall arc determines analogous maximal-cycle pockets of the wall color. Conditional on the path and the exterior pocket data, all these pockets have independent homogeneous laws. A point wound by a containing contour or side closure, and farther than $O(\delta)$ from its bank walk, lies in one of the corresponding pockets. Every further contour winding that point is contained in that pocket.
  - Explanation: Reveals contour and maximal-cycle pocket data from outside and identifies independent homogeneous interior laws.
- **claim-zero-offset-moment-order** (bound, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-moment-comparison)): Let $\mathcal D_-$ and $\mathcal D_+$ be two families of homogeneous discrete disks of the same wall color. Suppose that each disk of $\mathcal D_-$ is contained in a disk of $\mathcal D_+$. Assume all disks lie in a fixed bounded region. For distinct points $z_1,\ldots,z_m$ in the smaller interiors, $$\mathbb E\prod_{j=1}^m H_{\mathcal D_-}(z_j) \ \leq\ \mathbb E\prod_{j=1}^m H_{\mathcal D_+}(z_j)+o(1). \label{q4pocket:moment-order}$$ The error tends to zero with the mesh, uniformly when the points have fixed positive pairwise separation. The statement compares moments, not signed heights in an ordered coupling.
  - Explanation: Compares sign-averaged moments through same-color disk inclusion without claiming an ordered coupling of signed heights.
- **claim-endpoint-status-disk-geometry** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-geometry)): For every positive-diameter limiting contour, and for the limiting distinguished path, the set of distinct multiple visits in the original-domain interior has Hausdorff dimension at most zero. Deterministic interior points are almost surely avoided. At every interior trace point there are disks of each winding status arbitrarily nearby. In the marked case the statuses are read after closing the path on either wall arc. No nonconstant subtraversal of a limit lies entirely on the original Jordan boundary.* *These statements and curve tightness hold both for the regular wall experiments and for the marked Jordan approximations in the theorem.
  - Explanation: Establishes tightness, status disks, point avoidance and restrictions on interior multiple visits and boundary traversal for endpoint experiments.
- **claim-protected-outer-comparisons** (construction, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-protected-cuts)): Let $L_n$ be simple discrete contour closures in a bounded Jordan domain $V$, converging uniformly modulo reparametrization to $L$. The closures may include one original wall arc. Assume the geometric properties of Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:geometry" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:geometry">87</a>. Let $T$ be the trace of $L$, and let $U$ and $E$ be, respectively, the open sets of winding status one and zero off $T$, with infinity in $E$. Then the components of $U$ are simply connected pointed kernels of the interiors of $L_n$.* *For every $\beta>0$ there exist simple regular comparison polygons $B_j$, and protecting balls centered on $T\cap V$ or $\partial V$, such that:* 1. *the pointed kernels of $B_j$ at points of $U$ are precisely the separate components of $U$;* 2. *every compact subset of $U$ is eventually contained in $B_j$;* 3. *at each fixed $j$, deleting the part of a sufficiently fine discrete pocket outside $B_j$ changes edges only in finitely many protecting balls, of radii $r_i$, with $\sum_i r_i^\beta\longrightarrow0$ as $j\to\infty$;* 4. *$B_j$ is connected to a region outside $\overline V$.* *The finite protecting selection is made after constructing the cuts.
  - Explanation: Separates winding components as pointed kernels and constructs protected regular outer polygons without filling their distinct components together.
- **claim-rough-interior-moment-transfer** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-rough-transfer)): Condition on exterior pocket data converging to a containing contour as in Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:protected-cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:protected-cuts">88</a>. At every fixed distinct tuple of points in $U$, the joint moments of the residual zero-offset height converge to the Wick moments of independent fields $\sigma\Phi^0_\Omega$ in the components $\Omega$ of $U$. This holds along every such convergent sequence of exterior data. Several containing contours at one generation may be treated simultaneously, taking the product over them.
  - Explanation: Identifies conditional residual moments in rough winding components through protected outer cuts and regular inner comparisons.
- **claim-global-conditional-field-decomposition** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-conditional-field)): Conditional on the stated limiting exterior data, the height has the distributional decomposition $$h\ \stackrel{\mathrm{law}}=\ v+\sigma\sum_{\Omega\in\mathcal O}\Phi^0_\Omega, \label{q4pocket:conditional-decomposition}$$ where the Dirichlet fields are independent and extended by zero. The identity holds as an identity of distributions on the whole initial-domain interior, not merely after restriction to individual components.
  - Explanation: Identifies the conditional field globally as the component offsets plus independent zero-boundary fields, excluding an extra trace-supported distribution.
- **claim-bounded-thin-local-sets** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-local-set)): For the first contour level in the square, let $$A=\overline V\setminus\bigcup_{\Omega\in\mathcal O}\Omega.$$ In the marked experiment let $A$ be the path trace together with $\partial V$. After the normalizations below, these are bounded-type thin local sets. In the homogeneous case their harmonic values are $\pm2\lambda_0$. In the marked case their *total* harmonic values are $\pm\lambda_0$.
  - Explanation: Verifies locality, bounded harmonic values, thinness and the needed topology for the normalized contour and marked sets.
- **claim-regular-endpoint-chordal-limit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-regular-chordal)): The distinguished curves in the regular two-arc experiments converge as ordered curves, up to increasing changes of parametrization, to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_4$ between the prescribed marks.
  - Explanation: Uses boundary-data local-set uniqueness and geometric visit control to identify the full ordered regular marked curve.
- **claim-signed-square-contour-hierarchy** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-square-cle)): In a homogeneous square, the entire signed contour hierarchy converges to nested $\mathrm{CLE}_4$, with independent fair signs at each generation. The identification includes each individual contour as a simple-loop element, its parent, and its traversal order up to the loop convention.
  - Explanation: Identifies individual simple contours, signs, parents and traversal order throughout the nested endpoint hierarchy.
- **claim-endpoint-whole-plane-loops** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-whole-plane)): The infinite-volume free critical FK loop ensemble at $q=4$ converges to the nested whole-plane $\mathrm{CLE}_4$ ensemble, in the spherical matching metric for all loops.
  - Explanation: Transfers the endpoint square hierarchy to the free infinite-volume ensemble in the spherical matching topology.
- **claim-endpoint-marked-jordan-limit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4pocket-jordan-chordal)): For every marked uniform Jordan approximation specified in the theorem, its critical $q=4$ distinguished curve converges to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_4$ in the limiting marked domain.
  - Explanation: Transfers ordered endpoint interface convergence to the prescribed marked Jordan wired/free convention through actual-wall comparisons.

        "anchor": "stmt-cur-slab-estimate",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose a diagonal-time slab of macroscopic thickness about a low or high stencil contains no other non-diagonal tensors or endpoints. Diagonal chains may cross the slab. The stencil has an intact neighborhood disjoint from all other chains except its own prefix, and the slab has spare margins for routing and cuts. Bounded lattice errors are permitted inside these margins. Then the stencil contraction can be written as the corresponding low or high expression in Theorem <a href=\"#bulk:angular-estimate\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"bulk:angular-estimate\">15</a>, between exterior states independent of the choice of stencil term. Only boundedly many compensating pairs of rows and a common bounded scalar are introduced.*\n\n*In particular, if the two clear parts of the slab contain at least $n$ physical steps, its scalar contraction is bounded by $Cn^{-1+\\rho}$ for a low stencil, and by $Cn^{-1-\\rho}$ for a high stencil, times the two exterior reflection norms. Reflected stencils satisfy the same statement.",

        "exact_quote": "Let a four-change strand in $V_n$ be stopped before completing its strand, revealing only the switches it has encountered.         "exact_quote": "Let $u_n$ be the horizontal coordinate of the conformal rectangle map of $U_n$, with the designated primal arcs at $0$ and $1$.         "anchor": "stmt-moving-flags",
        "exact_quote": "In a fixed bulk block let $\\pi$ be a simple known primal bank path. Choose fixed scales $\\ell\\ll R_1$, away from its endpoints and the original boundary. Flag a deterministic grid cell of side $\\ell$ if, in its annulus from $100\\ell$ to $R_1$, the prefix already supplies four cyclically alternating actual arms, its two primal arms being known wired bank paths. If a candidate within $O(\\ell)$ of this cell actually connects to an electrode, then six actual alternating arms occur in a cropped annulus from $200\\ell$ to $R_1/2$. For a bounded region covered by the deterministic cells, the averaged conditional attachment cost of all flagged cells is at most $$\\label{moving:flag-sum}\n C\\ell^{-2}(\\ell/R_1)^{2+c_0}=O_{R_1}(\\ell^{c_0}).$$ The statement remains valid with one initial test step and with the bounded cap changes in <a href=\"#moving:odds\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"moving:odds\">[moving:odds]</a>.",

        "anchor": "stmt-q4field-moment-kernels",
        "exact_quote": "For the regular polygons just specified, the height moment kernels at distinct interior points $z_1,\\ldots,z_m$ satisfy $$\\label{q4field:log-kernel}\n \\left|\\mathbb E\\prod_{i=1}^m h_\\delta(z_i)\\right|\n \\le C_m\\bigl(1+|\\log(d_*\\vee\\delta)|\\bigr)^m,\n \\qquad d_*=1\\wedge\\min_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|,$$ with $d_*=1$ when $m=1$. Here $C_m$ depends on $V$ and $m$, uniformly over the interior tuples, including those approaching the boundary. Geometric majorants for the conditional signed expansions have higher polynomial moments with corresponding logarithmic bounds. Integrated moments are uniformly integrable; the height laws are tight as local distributions, and their moment kernels are asymptotically equicontinuous on compact sets of distinct interior tuples. The count bounds hold also for arbitrarily shaped homogeneous walls in a fixed bounded box and for products of disks of one wall color.",

        "anchor": "stmt-q4pocket-discrete-pockets",
        "exact_quote": "In a homogeneous $C$-wall disk, each outer contour is the external perimeter of an outermost actual $C'$-cluster. Behind it lie pockets bounded by the maximal simple $C'$-open cycles, ordered by inclusion of their interiors. Their interiors are disjoint; several pockets can belong to one outer contour. The contours, these cycles, their assignment to contours, and all switches outside the pocket interiors can be determined without querying strictly interior switches. Conditional on these data, the pocket interiors have independent homogeneous $C'$-wall laws.*\n\n*In a two-arc disk, first reveal the distinguished path. On either side, its bank together with that side’s wall arc determines analogous maximal-cycle pockets of the wall color. Conditional on the path and the exterior pocket data, all these pockets have independent homogeneous laws. A point wound by a containing contour or side closure, and farther than $O(\\delta)$ from its bank walk, lies in one of the corresponding pockets.
