<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Critical edge and continuum parameters** ([source](#intro:finite-law)): Fix a real number $q\in[1,4]$ and put $$\label{intro:parameters} p_q=\frac{\sqrt q}{1+\sqrt q}, \qquad \kappa(q)=\frac{4\pi}{\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)}.$$
- **Random-cluster probability law** ([source](#intro:finite-law)): The random-cluster law is $$\label{intro:finite-law} \phi_{G,q}^{\xi}(A) =\frac{1}{Z_{G,q}^{\xi}} p_q^{\|A\|}(1-p_q)^{\|E\|-\|A\|}q^{k_\xi(A)}.$$
- **Actual open path** ([source](#intro:finite-law)): An *actual open path* always consists of open edges of $G$.
- **Marked uniform Jordan approximation** ([source](#intro:marked-jordan)): For two marked boundary points $a,b$, we require counterclockwise parametrizations $\beta_n,\beta:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$, injective on $[0,1)$, such that $$\begin{gathered} \label{intro:marked-jordan} \beta_n(0)=\beta_n(1)=a_n,\qquad \beta_n(1/2)=b_n,\qquad \beta(0)=\beta(1)=a,\qquad \beta(1/2)=b,\\ \sup_{t\in[0,1]}\|\beta_n(t)-\beta(t)\|\longrightarrow0.\notag \end{gathered}$$
- **Oriented uniform curve distance** ([source](#intro:curve-metric)): For continuous oriented curves $\gamma_1,\gamma_2:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$, write $$\label{intro:curve-metric} d_{\mathrm{curv}}(\gamma_1,\gamma_2) =\inf_{\varphi_1,\varphi_2} \sup_{0\le t\le1} \|\gamma_1(\varphi_1(t))-\gamma_2(\varphi_2(t))\|,$$ where the infimum is over increasing homeomorphisms of $[0,1]$.
- **Loop-collection matching** ([source](#intro:collections)): For two collections, an $\varepsilon$-matching is a partial bijection that covers all loops of spherical diameter greater than $\varepsilon$ in both collections, has matched-loop distance at most $\varepsilon$, and leaves only loops of diameter at most $\varepsilon$ unmatched.
- **Positive cap completion** ([source](#pm-h-14)): A *positive cap completion* joins the unmatched ports around the primal intervals in the added boundary disk.
- **One-sided logarithmic error allowance** ([source](#exp:error-convention)): For clarity, a one-sided error denoted $o(\log n)$ in an upper bound means an allowance $$\label{exp:error-convention} \varepsilon\log n+O_\varepsilon(1) \quad\text{for every fixed }\varepsilon>0.$$
- **Current path primitive** ([source](#pm-h-35)): Define its primitive $\mathcal J(\mathcal C)$ by summing over the choice of one marked step:
- **Open-cap law** ([source](#pm-h-39)): Under the *open-cap law*, the four unmatched ports remain open; every closed loop, including those closed by local caps, receives weight $d$, in addition to the common tile coefficients.
- **Corrected tree observable** ([source](#pm-h-40)): Set $$\Gamma(\mathfrak A)=P_0y^2,\qquad \Gamma(\mathfrak B)=-P_0y,\qquad H_V^\circ=H_V-\Gamma(\operatorname{col}(V))D_V. \label{four:corrected}$$
- **Homogeneous actual wall** ([source](#peel:construction)): More generally, a *homogeneous wall* of color $C\in\{{\sf P},{\sf D}\}$ consists of actual open $C$-edges and these deterministic triangles on its inward side.
- **Radial angular gap** ([source](#peel:radial)): Choose lifts so that $$\label{peel:angle} \theta_t=O_t-W_t\in[0,2\pi]$$ is the angle of the counterclockwise dual boundary arc.
- **Discrete exploration episode** ([source](#loop:episodes)): A discrete *episode* starts when a cap is opened and ends at the next switch retaining a homogeneous pocket.
- **Fair-signed domain height** ([source](#q4field:domain-height)): Conditional on the geometry, $$\label{q4field:domain-height} h_\delta(z)=u_{*,\delta}(z) +\sum_{L\text{ internal}}\epsilon_L \mathbf1_{\{z\in\operatorname{int}L\}},$$ where the signs are independent and fair.

| q-critical-edge-probability | Critical edge probability | = | $\frac{\sqrt q}{1+\sqrt q}$ | Each fixed parameter in the stated interval. |

| q-passage-exponential-moment | Conditional exponential passage moment | ≤ | $C_B$ | Each fixed exponential rate and fixed geometry. |

| q-high-angular-sandwich | High angular difference sandwich operator norm | ≤ | $Cn^{-1-\rho}$ | Fixed cluster parameter and strict compact angle interval. |
| q-plane-row-operator-bound | Normalized row operator norm | ≤ | $2\\|D\\|$ | Homogeneous normalized strict-angle rows. |
| q-mixed-derivative-decay | Mixed stencil magnitude | = | $O(n^{-2-c})$ | Gaps and finite reflection templates fixed before the mesh limit. |
| q-small-cross-ratio-asymptotic | Open-cap crossing probability | ~ | $c_q\chi^h$ | Cross-ratio tends to the stated endpoint with the cluster parameter fixed. |
| q-endpoint-motion-tail | Directed fast-motion probability near coincidence | ≤ | $C\exp(-cr/\sqrt u)+o(1)$ | Mesh limit first at fixed angular displacement and radial duration; reflected statement at the opposite endpoint. |
| q-gff-variance-normalization | Gaussian field variance multiplier | = | $\frac{2}{\pi}$ | Endpoint field normalization. |
| q-local-set-height-scale | Continuum local-set height scale | = | $\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{8}}$ | Endpoint unit-jump normalization. |
| q-endpoint-four-arm-upper-bound | Mesh-limit upper alternating four-arm probability | ≤ | $C(r/R)^2$ | Fixed radii before the mesh limit. |
| q-free-bank-arm-bound | Actual free-bank arm probability | ≤ | $C_0(r/R)^\beta$ | Uniform in mesh and remaining exterior data; also product free laws. |

          "exact_quote": "Fix a compact interval $I\\subset(-v,v)$. Let $B_{\\rm in}$ be a product of $P_\\zeta$ rows and $B_{\\rm out}$ a product of $P_\\xi$ rows, at real angles in $[-v,v]$. Suppose each product contains at least $n\\ge1$ angles in $I$. Uniformly for $x,y\\in[-v,v]$, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\|B_{\\rm out}N(x)B_{\\rm in}\\|&\\le Cn^{-1+\\rho},\n \\label{bulk:low-estimate}\\\\\n \\|B_{\\rm out}\\{N(x)-e^{i\\tau(x-y)}N(y)\\}B_{\\rm in}\\|\n &\\le Cn^{-1-\\rho}.\\label{bulk:high-estimate}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The constant depends on $q$ and $I$. Boundedly many additional pairs of before-twist rows may be inserted immediately to the right of $N$, and additional pairs of after-twist rows immediately to its left. The constant may depend on a bound for these counts. <a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-loop-law** [claim](#stmt-prelim-loop-law) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-loop-law): Euler perimeter count and the domain Markov property. -> Exact capped FK law.
- **step-finite-loops** [claim](#stmt-prelim-finite-loops) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-finite-loops): Successive actual primal and dual circuit screens. -> Finite plane loops and finite-surgery laws.
- **step-collar** [claim](#stmt-prelim-collar) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-collar): Extremal likelihood ratios and color screening searches. -> Bounded remote marginal densities.
- **step-relative-collar** [claim](#stmt-prelim-relative-collar) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-relative-collar): Couple a common marginal part and contract expectation intervals. -> Relative remote expectation contraction.
- **step-passages** [claim](#stmt-prelim-passages) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-passages): Explore actual components, then subdivide and apply conditional moment bounds. -> All fixed exponential passage moments.
- **step-tilts** [claim](#stmt-prelim-tilts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-tilts): Induct on nest levels using separated buffers and Hölder estimates. -> Stable tilt ratios and shell moments.
- **step-absorb** [claim](#stmt-prelim-absorb) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-absorb): Split at a logarithmic passage threshold and control the tail by Cauchy–Schwarz. -> Arbitrarily small polynomial perturbation cost.
- **step-surface** [claim](#stmt-prelim-surface) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-surface): Localize slit surgery weights through buffered patch ports. -> Separated slit partition comparison.
- **step-local-costs** [claim](#stmt-exp-local-costs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-local-costs): Compare cutoff conventions and extend or block actual arms. -> Stable logarithmic costs and strict arm decay.
- **step-cap-elimination** [claim](#stmt-exp-cap-elimination) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-cap-elimination): Remove innermost disk arcs while tracking high-low cap partners. -> Local cap and corner-nest factors.
- **step-log-budgets** [claim](#stmt-exp-comparisons) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-cap-elimination-2): Compare opposite winding expansions in a rectangle and the uncharged and charged cylinders. -> Flat, corner and charge logarithmic budgets.
- **step-polygon-budget** [claim](#stmt-exp-polygon-budget) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-polygon-budget): Solve the cyclic side-parity condition and pair convex and concave costs. -> Balanced approximants with strict boundary savings.
- **step-plane-kernels** [claim](#stmt-bulk-plane-kernels) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bulk-plane-kernels): Identify torus and cylinder local limits, then complete their positive Gram form. -> Separable plane row Hilbert space.
- **step-angle-generator** [claim](#stmt-bulk-boost) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bulk-boost): Represent exponentially convex angle correlations and close the analytic-vector generator. -> Self-adjoint generator and holomorphic rows.
- **step-edge-bands** [claim](#stmt-bulk-edge-band) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bulk-edge-band): Continue endpoint vacuum vectors and pass a common radius to scalar spectral fibers. -> Fixed zero-free scalar bands and strip contraction.
- **step-angular-estimate** [claim](#stmt-bulk-angular-estimate) / [proof](#pm-h-32): Factor scalar inner functions, glue low-band insertions, estimate Laurent modes and sum damped bands. -> Low and high angular sandwich rates.
- **step-current-deformation** [claim](#stmt-cur-deformation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cur-deformation): Cancel marker-gauge changes and paired tangency terms. -> Pairingwise path isotopy identity.
- **step-tree-evaluation** [claim](#stmt-cur-tree-weights) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cur-tree-weights): Cross separator arcs minimally and sum their orientations. -> Primitive and pure-string tree weights.
- **step-slab-extraction** [claim](#stmt-cur-slab-estimate) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cur-slab-estimate): Choose common endpoints, consolidate twists and preserve a common routing phase. -> Stencil extraction retaining exterior norms.
- **step-four-tree** [claim](#stmt-four-tree) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-tree): Attach the local cap annulus and evaluate the separator-tree path. -> Cap loop count, crossing alternatives and observable recursion.
- **step-four-marked** [claim](#stmt-four-marked) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-marked): Use the edge table, terminal cancellations and boundary line identities. -> Marked values and bounded corrected observable.
- **step-four-compactness** [claim](#stmt-four-compactness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-compactness): Bound terminal-leg passages and shield boundary points by opposite-color crosscuts. -> Moment compactness and boundary shielding.
- **step-four-residual** [claim](#stmt-four-residual) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-residual): Cancel a weighted diagonal string, then remove the positive weight by relative collar separation. -> Vanishing ordinary-boundary diagonal residual.
- **step-conditional-map** [claim](#stmt-four-conditional-map) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-conditional-map): Reflect boundary lines, control the reflex corner and apply the argument principle and Schwarz–Christoffel formula. -> Conditional target map and crossing formula.
- **step-distant-factor** [claim](#stmt-wall-distant) / [proof](#proof-stmt-wall-distant): Separate positive corridor loop factors from rare bad endpoint enclosures. -> Positive distant mean and bounded moments.
- **step-wall-factorization** [claim](#stmt-wall-factorization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-wall-factorization): Match inversion phases and decouple inner tree data from distant loop factors. -> Nonvanishing product factorization.
- **step-gap-closure** [claim](#stmt-gap-closure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gap-closure): Confine affected paths, eliminate local caps and relatively decouple the positive tip multiplier. -> Positive bounded gap-closing multiplier.
- **step-reflection-templates** [claim](#stmt-hol-templates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hol-templates): Purify folded cell labels, align copies with primary gaps and perturb a finite template. -> Finite templates with almost complete expected extraction.
- **step-mixed-saving** [claim](#stmt-hol-mixed-bound) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hol-mixed-bound): Combine extracted angular costs with averaged feature savings and the exact normalization. -> Strict mixed derivative decay.
- **step-holomorphic-limit** [claim](#stmt-hol-disk) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hol-disk): Sum stencil identities by parts, close gaps in order and use the nonconstant exterior factor. -> Holomorphic disk limits and unconditional polygon crossing formula.
- **step-jordan-transfer** [claim](#stmt-jordan-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jordan-transfer): Sandwich on a common physical grid between easier and harder rational polygon quads. -> Actual Jordan-quad crossing limit.
- **step-jordan-cardy** [claim](#stmt-jordan-cardy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jordan-cardy): Specialize the crossing formula where the partition no longer changes the edge law. -> Free-boundary bond crossing integral.
- **step-compatible-drawing** [claim](#stmt-moving-drawing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-moving-drawing): Use boundary-edge tabs and a thin collar while retaining actual bank accesses. -> Nearby simple drawing with exact conditional slit law.
- **step-interval-asymptotic** [claim](#stmt-moving-asymptotic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-moving-asymptotic): Transform the crossing integrals and evaluate their endpoint behavior. -> Complementary symmetry and positive small-interval asymptotic.
- **step-chart-modulus** [claim](#stmt-moving-chart-modulus) / [proof](#proof-stmt-moving-chart-modulus): Compare Brownian hitting and chart continua under localized marks. -> Uniform small-path chart modulus.
- **step-deletion-cost** [claim](#stmt-moving-deletion) / [proof](#proof-stmt-moving-deletion): Explore deletion endpoint clusters in a monotone coupling and dominate residual arms by wired rims. -> Vanishing protected-ball attachment costs.
- **step-flag-cost** [claim](#stmt-moving-flags) / [proof](#proof-stmt-moving-flags): Use optimistic no-bridge tests to force actual alternating arms and sum over deterministic cells. -> Small averaged flagged attachment cost.

          "exact_quote": "The number of loops closed by the local boundary caps is $$\\mathcal I=\\#\\{\\text{unwired tree vertices}\\}.\n \\label{four:loop-count}$$ Exactly one of $E_{\\mathfrak A},E_{\\mathfrak B}$ occurs. Completing the four open ports around $A,C$ adds respectively one and two loops on these events.*\n\n\n\n\n\n*For an edge $e$ represented by an arc $i\\to j$, $i<j$, put $$m_e=h_i-h_j,\\qquad\n w_e=\\frac{\\cos((m_e-\\tfrac12)\\lambda)}{\\sin\\lambda},\\qquad\n k_e=-\\frac{\\cos((m_e+\\tfrac12)\\lambda)}{\\sin\\lambda},\\qquad\n a_e=x^{h_i+h_j}.\n \\label{four:edge-weights}$$ Let $\\mathcal P(V)$ be the root-to-$V$ edge path. Define $$\\begin{aligned}\n D_V&=d^{-\\mathcal I}\\prod_{e\\in\\mathcal P(V)}k_e\n                         \\prod_{e\\notin\\mathcal P(V)}w_e,\\label{four:D}\\\\\n H_V&=d^{-\\mathcal I}\\sum_{e\\in\\mathcal P(V)}a_e\n       \\prod_{f\\text{ before }e\\text{ in }\\mathcal P(V)}k_f\n       \\prod_{f\\text{ not before }e,\\ f\\ne e}w_f.\n       \\label{four:H}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Thus $H_{\\rm root}=0$. If $e$ joins its parent $u$ to its child $v$, the common product $D_e^\\circ$, with the factor on $e$ omitted, satisfies $$H_v-H_u=a_eD_e^\\circ,\\qquad\n D_u=w_eD_e^\\circ,\\qquad D_v=k_eD_e^\\circ.\n \\label{four:recursion}$$",

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-critical-interface-limit**: At each fixed admissible cluster weight, the prescribed critical Dobrushin interface converges to chordal SLE in the uniform oriented-curve topology. The approximation must retain its marked boundary order.
- **invariant-loop-multiplicity-and-traversal**: The plane-loop limit retains distinct collection elements, complete traversals, and every nesting generation. Agreement of trace images alone does not establish the stated convergence.
- **invariant-actual-connectivity**: Boundary identifications determine component weights and cannot supply edges of an actual crossing path.
- **invariant-cardy-boundary-law**: The bond-percolation crossing limit uses independently sampled boundary edges and no wiring. Its event is actual connectivity between the prescribed closed boundary arcs.
- **invariant-endpoint-conditional-field**: At the endpoint, the conditional height decomposition holds on the whole initial-domain interior. Its complementary Dirichlet fields are independent, and the identity excludes an unrecorded distribution supported on the remaining trace.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-uniform-cluster-weight-tolerance**: Choose a common mesh accuracy across varying cluster weights by treating the convergence theorem as uniform in the parameter. -> The theorem supplies fixed-parameter convergence and does not provide the uniform error control needed for that tolerance.
- **anti-wire-jump-crossings**: Count vertices joined by a boundary partition as an actual open crossing between electrodes. -> A partition tie can change the configuration weight without producing any sampled edge path between the electrodes.
- **anti-identify-cap-normalizations**: Use the open-cap crossing probability unchanged for separately wired intervals. -> Deterministic cap completion reweights the pairing alternatives, so the crossing probability generally changes.
- **anti-conditioned-maze-six-arm-bound**: Apply the original-law six-arm estimate uniformly after conditioning on every explored slit domain. -> The moving-domain argument controls exceptional histories through averaged costs; it does not establish the proposed deterministic-history estimate.
- **anti-endpoint-by-strict-range-continuity**: Extend strict-range angular and six-arm estimates to the endpoint by continuity in the cluster weight. -> The endpoint uses a separate field argument, and the whole-plane field input alone does not identify finite-domain fields or explored interfaces.
- **anti-trace-only-loop-verification**: Verify loop convergence solely by comparing unions of curve images or filled interiors. -> Such comparisons can discard multiplicities and traversal order, which are part of the conclusion.
- **anti-infer-simple-endpoint-from-contact-dimension**: Infer that the endpoint limit is a simple SLE curve solely from the interior contact-dimension bound. -> A dimension bound on interior contacts does not identify the curve law or exclude boundary traversals and additional ordering defects.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The principal results identify probability laws through vanishing-mesh limits, infinite-volume limits, and continuum field and curve arguments. They do not state a finite constructive decision procedure or a finite-mesh error certificate. The main theorem explicitly states: “Both conclusions hold along every mesh sequence. No uniformity in $q$ is asserted.” A finite check of switch pairings or sampled configurations would cover only an auxiliary finite identity and would not decide these convergence assertions.

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-critical-square-lattice-regime** (hypothesis): The interface and loop conclusions require the specified critical square-lattice law with the cluster parameter fixed in the stated interval. Blocked use: ["Applying the conclusions to off-critical edge probabilities, arbitrary lattice embeddings, or cluster parameters outside the theorem's interval."]
- **limit-no-parameter-uniformity** (formal_scope): Full mesh-sequence convergence does not provide uniform convergence across cluster parameters or a common finite-mesh tolerance. Blocked use: ['Selecting a shared mesh resolution across varying cluster weights solely from the convergence theorem.', 'Reporting a certified numerical convergence rate without an additional quantitative argument.']
- **limit-marked-jordan-approximation** (hypothesis): The chordal result requires the prescribed uniform marked boundary approximation and boundary conventions; an interior domain limit alone does not establish these premises. Blocked use: ['Invoking chordal convergence after checking only interior kernel convergence.', 'Allowing boundary marks to merge or change their prescribed cyclic order.']
- **limit-actual-paths-versus-wiring** (formal_scope): Boundary partition identifications affect configuration weights and cannot serve as edges of an actual open path. Blocked use: ['Counting a boundary wire jump as an actual crossing between distinct electrodes.', 'Replacing actual cluster exploration by connectivity in a graph augmented with partition edges.']
- **limit-cardy-bond-boundary-convention** (hypothesis): The stated Cardy limit concerns independent bond edges, including every boundary edge, with no wiring. Blocked use: ['Using this theorem as a proof for site percolation.', 'Fixing free boundary edges or introducing external connections while retaining the same crossing contract.', 'Treating the limiting integral as an exact finite-graph probability.']
- **limit-distinct-probability-spaces** (formal_scope): The finite Dobrushin and free infinite-volume experiments have separate convergence conclusions and need no coupling between their sampled configurations. Blocked use: ['Inferring a particular joint coupling of the finite interface and infinite-volume loop ensemble from the main theorem.', 'Using the whole-plane loop law as the unmodified loop law in an arbitrary bounded container.']
- **limit-full-loop-elements** (formal_scope): The collection conclusion retains individual loop elements, multiplicities and complete traversals through the prescribed spherical matching topology. Blocked use: ['Certifying collection convergence from proximity of unions of images.', 'Merging distinct loops with coincident images.', 'Discarding nesting generations or ignoring traversal order.']
- **limit-collar-screening-geometry** (hypothesis): The bounded-density and relative collar comparisons require their common graph, compatible deterministic wires and specified screening geometry. Blocked use: ['Transferring remote density bounds across collars with uncontrolled through-wire blocks or identifications that bypass the collar.', 'Applying relative contraction to an arbitrary collection of sectors.']
- **limit-error-absorption-moments** (hypothesis): Absorption of passage factors requires a positive expectation lower bound, a polynomial second-moment bound and exponential passage moments at every fixed rate. Blocked use: ['Absorbing an error when the observable denominator may vanish.', 'Replacing all fixed exponential moment bounds by an unproved tail assumption.']
- **limit-slit-partitions-not-pointwise-densities** (formal_scope): The isolated-slit polarity comparison controls partition functions rather than a bounded configurationwise density for changing an entire wall. Blocked use: ['Converting the slit partition comparison into an arbitrary-event density bound for simultaneous changes of all wall pairings.']
- **limit-strict-range-endpoint-separation** (formal_scope): The endpoint requires its separate height-field and geometric arguments; strict angular and six-arm estimates are not extended there by continuity. Blocked use: ['Taking the endpoint limit inside strict-range angular estimates.', 'Using a boundary crossing input at the endpoint outside its stated range.', 'Inferring finite-domain or conditional interface convergence directly from the whole-plane field input.']
- **limit-extraction-exterior-norms** (hypothesis): Clear-slab extraction needs the specified vacant margins and intact stencil neighborhood, and its scalar estimates retain both exterior reflection norms. Blocked use: ['Applying the extraction estimate across other non-diagonal insertions or endpoints.', 'Dropping exterior reflection norms from a scalar bound.', 'Treating local extraction as uniform control of arbitrary boundary states.']
- **limit-conditional-conformal-map** (hypothesis): The target-map identification is conditional on holomorphicity until that premise is established for the specified balanced rational polygons. Blocked use: ['Using boundary values and compactness alone as proof of holomorphicity.', 'Applying the conditional conformal-map proposition to an arbitrary continuous subsequential observable.']
- **limit-cap-normalization-reweighting** (formal_scope): Open-cap and deterministic separate-cap crossing probabilities have distinct outcome weights. Blocked use: ['Using the open-cap probability unchanged for a separately wired crossing experiment.']
- **limit-auxiliary-limit-order** (hypothesis): Geometry and auxiliary parameters remain fixed through the mesh limit and are removed only in the prescribed order. Blocked use: ['Shrinking wall gaps with the mesh without a separate uniform estimate.', 'Interchanging distant-charge removal, gap closure and mesh limits.', 'Assuming the comparison multipliers themselves converge.']
- **limit-localized-averaged-history-tests** (hypothesis): Moving-domain tests require localized basepoint and prime-end data and provide convergence in probability over histories rather than a deterministic estimate for every explored maze. Blocked use: ['Applying the moving test when the basepoint disk degenerates or marked prime ends collide.', 'Conditioning the original six-arm estimate on every possible explored domain.', 'Replacing averaged conditional error control by a historywise bound.']
- **limit-driving-versus-ordered-trace** (formal_scope): Driving convergence requires additional physical compactness and traversal arguments to identify the entire ordered curve, including capacity plateaus and the target tail. Blocked use: ['Declaring uniform physical curve convergence solely from convergence of Loewner drivers.', 'Discarding a possible swallowed excursion or repeated traversal without the separate geometric argument.']
- **limit-branch-separation-and-causal-conditioning** (formal_scope): Branch continuations become independent after target-kernel separation; earlier shared exploration and conditioning on the common causal past remain essential. Blocked use: ['Assigning independent branch noises before the targets separate.', 'Conditioning continuation laws on future separation information or terminal bracket values.']
- **limit-loop-identification-near-square-wall** (edge_case): The strict-range intermediate loop identification gives equality as curves when either matched element stays away from the square wall; the unrestricted intermediate conclusion is ordered containment. Blocked use: ['Promoting the intermediate bounded-square identification to equality of all boundary-touching loop elements before the escape comparison.']
- **limit-endpoint-field-tests-and-normalization** (hypothesis): The whole-plane endpoint height uses independent fair unit jumps and neutral smooth tests with the prescribed Green normalization. Blocked use: ['Applying the whole-plane height conclusion to arbitrary pointwise heights or nonneutral tests without fixing an additive constant.', 'Changing loop-sign dependence or jump normalization while retaining the same continuum multiplier.']
- **limit-endpoint-relative-four-arm-errors** (approximation): The endpoint four-arm coefficient argument needs error bounds relative to the product of the retained arm costs; an absolute vanishing error is insufficient. Blocked use: ['Replacing the relative tail or support-hit controls by an absolute error before deriving the arm bound.']
- **limit-interior-contact-dimension** (formal_scope): The endpoint contact-dimension bound concerns genuinely distinct interior macroscopic visits after constant pauses are discarded and makes no boundary-contact assertion. Blocked use: ['Inferring absence of all self-contacts from a dimension bound.', 'Using the contact bound alone to identify a simple ordered interface.', 'Extending the interior estimate to boundary contacts.']
- **limit-free-bank-local-premise** (hypothesis): Free-bank passage and arm bounds require the selected bank color to have no forced open edge or boundary identification on walls meeting the patch. Blocked use: ['Applying free-bank domination across a patch containing a forced same-color wall path or same-color wall ties.']
- **limit-moment-comparison-not-height-order** (formal_scope): The pocket comparison orders zero-offset moments for contained disk families of the same wall color; it does not order signed heights in a coupling. Blocked use: ['Claiming pointwise monotonicity of signed heights or nesting depths in the original edgewise coupling.', 'Comparing disk families with unmatched wall colors using this lemma.']
- **limit-protected-components-and-global-field** (formal_scope): Rough-domain transfer preserves separate winding components and must establish the conditional field as a distribution on the whole domain. Blocked use: ['Filling a limiting contour hull and joining separate winding components.', 'Inferring the global conditional identity from componentwise restrictions while leaving an unexamined trace-supported distribution.']
- **limit-continuum-identification-not-finite-certificate** (nonconstructive): The principal convergence results depend on continuum limits, Hilbert-space completion and stochastic or local-set uniqueness. Finite enumeration can check auxiliary configurations but cannot certify these complete convergence conclusions. Blocked use: ['Presenting an auxiliary finite identity check as certification of the interface or nested-ensemble scaling limit.', 'Claiming an exact continuum sampler or finite-mesh error certificate from the main convergence theorem alone.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For every fixed $`1\le q\le4`$, critical square-lattice random-cluster Dobrushin interfaces converge to chordal $`\mathop{\mathrm{SLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}`$, where $`\kappa(q)=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)`$, and the complete nested plane loop collections converge to whole-plane $`\mathop{\mathrm{CLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}`$. The results hold under uniform marked Jordan boundary approximation and retain loop multiplicities and traversals. At <i>q</i> = 1 we obtain Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction and precise statements

Planar critical models are expected to have conformally invariant scaling limits. For random-cluster models this prediction identifies the law of an interface, the joint law of all surrounding loops, and crossing probabilities in arbitrary shapes. These are distinct conclusions: a limit for one interface does not by itself identify its coupling with other interfaces, and convergence of loop traces on compact sets does not by itself retain multiplicities, nesting, or complete traversals.

Schramm’s characterization of conformally invariant interfaces led to Schramm–Loewner evolution (Schramm 2000) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Schramm2000](#ref-Schramm2000)]. Cardy’s prediction for critical percolation crossings (Cardy 1992) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Cardy1992](#ref-Cardy1992)] was proved by Smirnov for site percolation on the triangular lattice (Smirnov 2001) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[Smirnov2001](#ref-Smirnov2001)]. The random-cluster Ising model has a discrete holomorphic observable (Smirnov 2010) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Smirnov2010](#ref-Smirnov2010)], and its interface convergence is established in Chelkak et al. (2014) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[ChelkakDCHonglerKemppainenSmirnov2014](#ref-ChelkakDCHonglerKemppainenSmirnov2014)]. Conformal loop ensembles provide the corresponding continuum laws for complete families of interfaces (Sheffield and Werner 2012; Sheffield 2009) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[SheffieldWerner2012](#ref-SheffieldWerner2012), [Sheffield2009Exploration](#ref-Sheffield2009Exploration)]. The results below concern the nearest-neighbor square lattice, with its ordinary Euclidean embedding and its original random-cluster probability law.

<a id="intro:model"></a>
#### The model and its boundary conventions

<a id="intro:finite-law"></a>
Fix a real number $q\in[1,4]$ and put <a id="intro:parameters"></a>$$\label{intro:parameters}
 p_q=\frac{\sqrt q}{1+\sqrt q},
 \qquad
 \kappa(q)=\frac{4\pi}{\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)}.$$ The inverse cosine has values in $[0,\pi]$. Thus $4\le\kappa(q)\le6$, with $\kappa(1)=6$ and $\kappa(4)=4$. On a finite graph $G=(V,E)$, let $\xi$ be a partition of designated boundary vertices. For $A\subseteq E$, let $k_\xi(A)$ be the number of components of $(V,A)$ after identification within each block of $\xi$, including isolated vertices. The random-cluster law is $$\label{intro:finite-law}
 \phi_{G,q}^{\xi}(A)
 =\frac{1}{Z_{G,q}^{\xi}}
 p_q^{|A|}(1-p_q)^{|E|-|A|}q^{k_\xi(A)}.$$ An *actual open path* always consists of open edges of $G$. Identification in $\xi$ is used to compute the probability weight and does not supply an additional edge in such a path.

Let $D$ be a bounded Jordan domain. A lattice approximation at mesh $\delta_n\downarrow0$ is the bounded interior $D_n$ of a simple closed nearest-neighbor polygon on $\delta_n\mathbb Z^2$. Its graph $G_n$ has every lattice vertex in $\overline{D_n}$ and every nearest-neighbor edge whose closed segment is contained in $\overline{D_n}$. In particular, boundary edges are part of $G_n$.

<a id="intro:marked-jordan"></a>
For two marked boundary points $a,b$, we require counterclockwise parametrizations $\beta_n,\beta:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$, injective on $[0,1)$, such that $$\begin{gathered}
\label{intro:marked-jordan}
 \beta_n(0)=\beta_n(1)=a_n,\qquad \beta_n(1/2)=b_n,\qquad
 \beta(0)=\beta(1)=a,\qquad \beta(1/2)=b,\\
 \sup_{t\in[0,1]}|\beta_n(t)-\beta(t)|\longrightarrow0.\notag
\end{gathered}$$ The free arc $F_n$ goes counterclockwise from $a_n$ to $b_n$; the other arc $W_n$ goes counterclockwise from $b_n$ to $a_n$. Wire together all vertices of $W_n$, including the two marked endpoints. All other boundary vertices remain singleton blocks. Remove from the sampled edge set the boundary edges of $W_n$ and declare those edges open for the interface drawing. This is equivalent on all remaining edges to <a href="#intro:finite-law" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:finite-law">[intro:finite-law]</a> with the same wired partition: the endpoints of each removed edge were already identified. Edges on $F_n$ remain random.

The medial graph has vertices at the midpoints of primal edges, with medial edges joining the midpoints of consecutive sides of a lattice square. At an open primal edge the four incident medial half-edges are paired in quarter turns around the adjacent dual faces; at a closed primal edge they are paired around the primal endpoints. At the boundary one uses the turns between the primal wired arc and its complementary dual wired arc. There is a unique medial strand between the two changes of boundary condition. We orient it from $a_n$ to $b_n$ and denote it by $\eta_n$. This is the usual Dobrushin construction (Duminil-Copin 2017, sec. 5.2.2) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[DC2017Lectures](#ref-DC2017Lectures)]. Occurrence order at a twice-visited medial vertex is part of the curve. The tile drawings used later preserve this order and differ from the straight medial drawing by at most a constant times $\delta_n$ in uniform curve distance.

<a id="intro:curve-metric"></a>
For continuous oriented curves $\gamma_1,\gamma_2:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$, write $$\label{intro:curve-metric}
 d_{\mathrm{curv}}(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)
 =\inf_{\varphi_1,\varphi_2}
   \sup_{0\le t\le1}
   |\gamma_1(\varphi_1(t))-\gamma_2(\varphi_2(t))|,$$ where the infimum is over increasing homeomorphisms of $[0,1]$. Zero-distance curves are identified. Chordal $\operatorname{SLE}_\kappa$ in $(D;a,b)$ is the conformal image of the upper-half-plane Loewner trace driven by $\sqrt\kappa B_t$ from $0$ to $\infty$, with $B$ a standard Brownian motion. The remaining positive dilation of the conformal coordinate does not change this law.

<a id="intro:collections"></a>
#### Complete loop collections

Let $\phi_q^0$ be the weak limit of <a href="#intro:finite-law" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:finite-law">[intro:finite-law]</a> in increasing square boxes of $\mathbb Z^2$ with free boundary conditions. Form its complete medial interface collection, using the same local pairings as above, and then scale the embedding by $\delta$. Denote the resulting collection by $\Gamma_\delta$. It contains every loop at every nesting level. The elementary circuit argument in Section <a href="#sec:preliminaries" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:preliminaries">2</a> shows that its discrete interfaces are almost surely finite, also at $q=4$.

Individual loops are unrooted and unoriented continuous maps of the circle into the Riemann sphere $\widehat\mathbb C$. Their distance is the infimum of the uniform spherical distance over circular orientation-preserving homeomorphisms and reversal, with zero-distance representatives identified. We retain distinct loops even when their images coincide. For two collections, an $\varepsilon$-matching is a partial bijection that covers all loops of spherical diameter greater than $\varepsilon$ in both collections, has matched-loop distance at most $\varepsilon$, and leaves only loops of diameter at most $\varepsilon$ unmatched. Convergence of collections means the existence of such matchings with $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. The continuum law in the next statement is the standard nested whole-plane $\operatorname{CLE}_\kappa$ in this topology.

<a id="stmt-intro-main"></a>
<div id="intro:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1** (Interfaces and all nested loops). *For every fixed real $1\le q\le4$, the following assertions hold.*

1.  *For every bounded Jordan domain $D$ with distinct boundary marks $a,b$, and every approximation satisfying <a href="#intro:marked-jordan" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:marked-jordan">[intro:marked-jordan]</a>, the Dobrushin strand $\eta_n$ converges in law, in <a href="#intro:curve-metric" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:curve-metric">[intro:curve-metric]</a>, to chordal $\operatorname{SLE}_{\kappa(q)}$ from $a$ to $b$ in $D$.*

2.  *Under the specified free infinite-volume law, $\Gamma_\delta$ converges in law as $\delta\downarrow0$ to the nested whole-plane $\operatorname{CLE}_{\kappa(q)}$, in the spherical collection topology just defined. The limit is Möbius invariant.*

*Both conclusions hold along every mesh sequence. No uniformity in $q$ is asserted.*

</div>

Theorem <a href="#intro:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:main">1</a> establishes the SLE/CLE conformal-invariance prediction for critical random-cluster models on the square lattice throughout $q\in[1,4]$. The word “critical” refers to the edge parameter $p_q$. At $q=4$ the limits are chordal $\operatorname{SLE}_4$ and the standard simple nested whole-plane $\operatorname{CLE}_4$.

The endpoint proof uses a whole-plane height-field theorem, with its precise law and symmetry input verified in Section <a href="#sec:q4-rotation-repair" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:q4-rotation-repair">16</a>. That theorem supplies no finite-domain field convergence, conditional convergence after an exploration, or interface convergence. Sections <a href="#sec:q4regular" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:q4regular">18</a>– <a href="#sec:q4identification" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:q4identification">20</a> prove these further implications. The strict angular and six-arm estimates used for $q<4$ are not extended to $q=4$ by a limiting argument.

<a id="intro:crossings"></a>
#### Square-lattice bond crossings

For four distinct counterclockwise boundary marks $a,b,c,d$ of $D$, require the same uniform convergence as in <a href="#intro:marked-jordan" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:marked-jordan">[intro:marked-jordan]</a>, with the respective four marks at parameters $0,1/4,1/2,3/4$. Sample *all* edges of $G_n$ independently with probability $1/2$, including every boundary edge, and make no identifications or external connections. Let $C_n$ be the event of an actual open path from the closed counterclockwise arc $[a_n,b_n]$ to the closed counterclockwise arc $[c_n,d_n]$.

<a id="stmt-intro-cardy"></a>
<div id="intro:cardy" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2** (Cardy’s formula for square-lattice bond percolation). *Let $\psi:D\to\mathbb H$ send $a,c,d$ to $0,1,\infty$, and put $x=\psi(b)\in(0,1)$. Under the boundary and approximation conventions above, <a id="intro:cardy-formula"></a>$$\label{intro:cardy-formula}
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P(C_n)
 =\frac{\displaystyle\int_0^x[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,\mathrm dt}
        {\displaystyle\int_0^1[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,\mathrm dt}.$$*

</div>

Theorem <a href="#intro:cardy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:cardy">2</a> proves the square-lattice bond-percolation form of Cardy’s prediction with the free-boundary convention specified here. We obtain it directly from the alternating four-change calculation and a deterministic comparison on a common lattice graph. In particular, its proof supplies the boundary transfer for the actual crossing event; it does not infer continuity of that event from a curve limit.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
#### Proof structure and technical contributions

<a id="intro:fourchange-formula"></a>
For $1\le q<4$, use the parameters <a id="intro:lambda-rho"></a>$$\label{intro:lambda-rho}
 d=\sqrt q=2\cos\lambda,\qquad
 \rho=\lambda/\pi,\qquad 0<\lambda\le\pi/3.$$ The first part of the proof is a four-change boundary calculation. In the upper half-plane, put the boundary changes at $0,\chi,1,\infty$. For the open cap normalization, in which the four unmatched ends carry no additional pairing weights, the connection probability is $$\label{intro:fourchange-formula}
 f(\chi)=\frac{I_C(\chi)}{I_B(\chi)+I_C(\chi)},
 \quad
 \begin{cases}
 I_B(\chi)=\displaystyle\int_\chi^1
 u^{\rho-1}|u-\chi|^{\rho-1}|u-1|^{1-3\rho}\,\mathrm du,\\[3pt]
 I_C(\chi)=\displaystyle\int_1^\infty
 u^{\rho-1}|u-\chi|^{\rho-1}|u-1|^{1-3\rho}\,\mathrm du.
 \end{cases}$$ Separate deterministic cap wires on the two designated intervals change this to $f/(f+d(1-f))$. Keeping these two normalizations distinct is essential when $d\ne1$.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
###### Positive comparisons before complex observables.

Section <a href="#sec:preliminaries" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:preliminaries">2</a> identifies the capped tile law exactly with the random-cluster law and establishes the collar and passage-count comparisons used later. It keeps actual components distinct from boundary partition blocks. Bulk box crossing at $q\le4$ and the stronger up-to-boundary crossing estimates for $q<4$ have different roles (Duminil-Copin, Li, and Manolescu 2018; Duminil-Copin, Manolescu, and Tassion 2021) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[DCLM2019Isoradial](#ref-DCLM2019Isoradial), [DMT2021Fractal](#ref-DMT2021Fractal)]. Section <a href="#sec:exponents" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:exponents">3</a> derives the local exponent inequalities needed to control corner, tip, and source factors. All complex currents are subsequently estimated in these positive laws.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
###### Angular transfer and boundary holomorphicity.

Sections <a href="#sec:angular" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:angular">4</a> and <a href="#sec:current" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:current">5</a> construct the transfer operators, their reflected norms, and the path-current primitive. The argument distinguishes a common complex continuation radius from norm constants that may depend on a vector in the cyclic core. A scalar spectral factorization then suppresses the angular modes that would obstruct holomorphicity. The boundary calculation in Section <a href="#sec:fourchange" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:fourchange">6</a> is initially conditional on this holomorphicity. Sections <a href="#sec:pairedwall" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:pairedwall">7</a>–<a href="#sec:holomorphic" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:holomorphic">9</a> discharge the condition by a distant-probe comparison, closing finitely many wall gaps, and a folded mixed-stencil estimate. The folds retain the external states in their reflected norms; local exponent savings pay for extraction and normalization costs. This produces <a href="#intro:fourchange-formula" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:fourchange-formula">[intro:fourchange-formula]</a> without assuming a lattice conformal invariance theorem.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
###### Moving domains and the chordal driver.

The fixed-shape formula must remain useful after a random exploration. Section <a href="#sec:movingtests" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:movingtests">11</a> proves this transfer using a finite chart approximation and an averaged six-arm estimate under the original switch law. It does not require a uniform six-arm theorem in every possible explored domain. Section <a href="#sec:chordal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:chordal">12</a> first normalizes a shrinking test into a bounded martingale and then transfers it to the true Dobrushin law. Two tests identify the driver and its bracket. Tightness and a separate traversal argument give the Euclidean uniform curve conclusion of Theorem <a href="#intro:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:main">1</a>(i) for $q<4$.

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
###### Joint branches and loop identities.

Sections <a href="#sec:peeling" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:peeling">13</a>–<a href="#sec:loops" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:loops">15</a> construct a target tree by uniform-walled peeling. They establish the reflected angular dynamics, exclude forcepoint variation supported on endpoint times, and identify independent continuation noises after separation, conditional on the common causal history at separation. The resulting branching SLE description is then matched to the original discrete loops: winding information determines loop labels, while additional estimates determine full traversal order. An escape bound upgrades convergence in bounded windows to the spherical matching topology for every nesting generation.

<a id="pm-h-11"></a>
###### The endpoint field argument.

At $q=4$ the loop height uses independent fair signs and unit jumps. Section <a href="#sec:q4-rotation-repair" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:q4-rotation-repair">16</a> extracts a bijection of selected loops from the public FK homotopy coupling (Duminil-Copin, Kozlowski, Krachun, et al. 2026) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[DCKKMO2026Rotation](#ref-DCKKMO2026Rotation)]. Even sign moments depend only on loops that separate at least two distinct pairs of endpoints. These loops are macroscopic, and the bijection preserves their winding differences up to one harmless sign per loop. This supplies the endpoint symmetry input for the whole-plane six-vertex field theorem (Duminil-Copin, Kozlowski, Lammers, et al. 2026) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[SixVertexGFF2026](#ref-SixVertexGFF2026)], including the multiplicities that a loop-set distance alone would not determine. Section <a href="#sec:q4tools" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:q4tools">17</a> combines binary transport and reflection positivity with the whole-plane height input to control double contacts. The error estimates are relative to the square of the four-arm probability; an absolute error would be insufficient. Section <a href="#sec:q4regular" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:q4regular">18</a> derives the Dirichlet field in regular domains by translating separated charge groups and determining the harmonic boundary term. Section <a href="#sec:q4rough" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:q4rough">19</a> then treats rough explored pockets by a conditional moment comparison, with contour injections at each numerical nesting level and a regular-domain sandwich. The final identification verifies locality, thinness, bounded harmonic values, and the relevant topology before invoking two-valued local-set uniqueness (Aru, Sepúlveda, and Werner 2019; Aru, Lupu, and Sepúlveda 2020) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[AruSepulvedaWerner2019](#ref-AruSepulvedaWerner2019), [AruLupuSepulveda2020](#ref-AruLupuSepulveda2020)].

<a id="pm-h-12"></a>
#### Conventions on constants and limits

Every theorem is for a fixed $q$. Constants may depend on $q$, macroscopic shapes, positive separations, and an explicitly fixed finite set of tests. Mesh limits are taken with those data fixed; auxiliary separations, gaps, cutoffs, and localization parameters are removed in the stated order. A claim uniform over random exploration histories is made only where the corresponding comparison has been proved. In particular, convergence in probability over histories is not replaced by a deterministic estimate for every history.

The proof uses established public results at their stated hypotheses. It uses no theorem about an annealed random planar map, no random embedding, and no transfer from a random-map metric limit to the square lattice. The finite Dobrushin experiments and the free infinite-volume experiment are different probability spaces; the theorems assert their separate convergence and require no coupling between their samples.

<a id="sec:preliminaries"></a>
### Tiles, positive laws, and localization

Except where an endpoint statement is explicitly made, fix $1\le q<4$ and write <a id="prelim:parameters"></a>$$\label{prelim:parameters}
 d=\sqrt q=2\cos\lambda,\qquad \rho=\lambda/\pi,
 \qquad 0<\lambda\le\pi/3.$$ All constants may depend on this fixed parameter and on the fixed geometric shapes under consideration. In particular, none of the estimates below is asserted uniformly as $q\uparrow4$.

<a id="pm-h-14"></a>
#### Tiles and boundary caps

We use a square tile array whose corner sites alternate between primal ($\mathsf P$) and dual ($\mathsf D$) sites. The primal lattice consists of the primal diagonals, so its mesh is $\sqrt2$ times the tile-edge length. Rotating the tile coordinates gives the prescribed orientation of the primal square lattice. Each tile carries one of the two noncrossing pairings of its four side midpoints, called *ports*. Pairing around the dual corners declares the primal diagonal open; the other pairing declares the dual diagonal open. An *actual color path* uses these open diagonals and never uses boundary identifications as edges. A strand has an actual primal path on one side and an actual dual path on the other.

<figure id="prelim:switch-figure">

<figcaption>The two tile switches. The solid diagonal is an open primal edge; the dashed diagonal records the absent primal edge. The curved arcs specify the pairing of ports and hence the order of strand occurrences when a medial vertex is visited twice.</figcaption>
</figure>

<a id="pm-figsrc-prelim-switch-figure"></a>
**Figure source and visual witness** (`prelim:switch-figure`)

The left tile, labeled "primal open" below, has a solid diagonal line connecting the bottom-left P and top-right P corners, and two curved arcs: one pairing the top and left side midpoints (around top-left D), and one pairing the bottom and right side midpoints (around bottom-right D). The right tile, labeled "primal closed" below, has a dashed diagonal line connecting the bottom-left P and top-right P corners, and two curved arcs: one pairing the top and right side midpoints (around top-right P), and one pairing the bottom and left side midpoints (around bottom-left P).

For topological arguments, draw the two arcs of a switch disjointly within its tile, normally to the sides at their ports. This drawing and the straight medial drawing can be parametrized piece by corresponding piece, preserving the order of occurrences at a double visit. Their uniform distance is at most twice the tile diameter. Thus these local changes of drawing disappear in the curve topology of the theorem.

A wall cuts tile connections at ports. Distinct sectors at a wall corner have distinct copies of that corner, as on a surface cut open. The end of a finite slit has one sector of angle $2\pi$. All shapes in the tile arguments are unions of whole tiles; separating repeated boundary incidences by a small thickening leaves their combinatorics unchanged.

Partition each boundary component into intervals of alternating designated wire colors. Within an interval, pair the two intervening ports between successive occurrences of the designated color, including eligible end vertices. These are the *local caps*. A genuine change leaves one unmatched port, on the side whose color differs from the change vertex. Use the analogous cyclic caps on a boundary component without changes. Intervals will always be much longer than one mesh.

A *positive cap completion* joins the unmatched ports around the primal intervals in the added boundary disk. Equivalently, wire each primal interval separately, with a dual sea between these wires. This adds only boundedly many connections beyond the local caps when the number of changes is bounded. It adds no primal identification on a dual interval.

<a id="stmt-prelim-loop-law"></a>
<div id="prelim:loop-law" class="lemma">

**Lemma 3** (The positive loop law). *On a genus-zero tile surface with positive cap completions, the switch weight $d^\ell$, where $\ell$ counts completed medial loops, is proportional to the critical FK weight with the corresponding boundary partition. Conditional laws on common subdomains are therefore FK laws with induced partitions. The same assertion holds after interchanging the colors. On a torus without caps the two weights differ by a factor bounded in terms of $q$ alone.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prelim-loop-law"><summary>Proof of stmt-prelim-loop-law</summary>

*Proof.* Draw noncrossing exterior primal trees realizing the designated identifications and thicken the resulting open primal graph. Its perimeter is the medial loop collection, apart from a fixed number of exterior components. Euler’s formula gives the configuration-dependent part of the perimeter count as $$\ell=2k_\xi(A)+|A|+\text{constant}.$$ Since $d^2=q$ and $p_q/(1-p_q)=d$, the weights agree up to a constant independent of $A$. The domain Markov property gives the conditional-law statement. On a torus the thickened graph has Euler characteristic $|V|-|A|=2k-\ell-2g$, with $g\le1$, so the additional factor is bounded. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-15"></a>
#### Crossing estimates and finite plane loops

We use two distinct crossing inputs. The buffered bulk box-crossing theorem for canonical weights on doubly periodic isoradial graphs applies for $1\le q\le4$ (Duminil-Copin, Li, and Manolescu 2018, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[DCLM2019Isoradial](#ref-DCLM2019Isoradial)]. Square rhombi have canonical odds $\sqrt q$, so this includes our square lattice. For example, for fixed $a>0$, horizontal crossing of $[-an,an]\times[-n,n]$ inside $[-(a+1)n,(a+1)n]\times[-2n,2n]$ has probability bounded away from zero and one, uniformly in the boundary partition on the larger rectangle. The same theorem gives equality of the free and wired infinite-volume laws. Hence planar duality at these self-dual odds preserves the plane loop law, including when a tile translation exchanges the two colors.

When a crossing must reach a domain wall, we use the stronger theorem for critical square FK with $1\le q<4$: a discrete simple-polygon quad of bounded extremal distance has an actual open crossing with probability bounded away from zero, uniformly in its boundary partition (Duminil-Copin, Manolescu, and Tassion 2021, Theorem 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[DMT2021Fractal](#ref-DMT2021Fractal)]. We do not apply this statement at $q=4$. FKG and the domain Markov property apply because $q\ge1$; duality supplies the corresponding statements for the other color.

Here is the concrete wall application needed below. A tile-coordinate rectangle contains a nearest-neighbor quad of either color graph with staircase sides within boundedly many mesh layers of its boundary. For bounded aspect ratio its discrete extremal distance is bounded: there are order its width in mesh units disjoint zigzag paths, each of length at most a constant times its length; distributing a unit flow among them bounds the resistance. The geometric staircase quad likewise has bounded modulus. At an electrode on a wall, the last crossing vertex can be connected to a wall vertex of the same color using boundedly many fresh edges. Conditional finite energy bounds the extra cost below uniformly. Keep the electrode away from the ends of its designated wall interval.

Crossings in a buffered piecewise rectangular corridor follow by using strips of width a fixed fraction of its clearance and overlapping end squares. Transversal crossings in these squares join successive longitudinal crossings; FKG combines the finitely many requirements of one color. This constructs wall-to-wall paths in annular sectors with openings $\pi/2,\pi,3\pi/2,2\pi$, including between the two banks of a slit, as well as circuits in a full annulus. Different colors in tile-disjoint sectors can be imposed successively by their conditional lower bounds. All paths here are actual paths. Radii may use tile sup-norm rims, and all buffers have fixed relative width and sufficiently large fixed mesh width.

<a id="stmt-prelim-finite-loops"></a>
<div id="prelim:finite-loops" class="lemma">

**Lemma 4** (Finiteness in the plane). *For every $1\le q\le4$, all medial strands of the specified free infinite-volume square FK law are almost surely finite loops. Finite deterministic surgeries admit positive normalized loop laws with the FK conditional laws of Lemma <a href="#prelim:loop-law" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:loop-law">3</a>.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prelim-finite-loops"><summary>Proof of stmt-prelim-finite-loops</summary>

*Proof.* Buffered bulk crossing gives a conditional probability bounded below for an actual primal circuit around any fixed box in each of successively separated annuli. The probability of missing the first $m$ such screens is at most $(1-c)^m$, regardless of the exterior partition. The same argument gives arbitrarily large actual dual circuits. These two colors of screens prevent a medial strand meeting the box from escaping to infinity. Taking the countable union over boxes proves finiteness.

A surgery at finitely many tile connections changes only finitely many loops at a fixed mesh. Relative to the unmodified plane law, its weight ratio is $d^{\Delta\ell}$, bounded above and below by constants that may depend on this finite set of connections. Normalization defines its positive law. Equivalently, exhaust by planar domains; the same circuit argument makes the local completion independent of remote boundaries. Lemma <a href="#prelim:loop-law" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:loop-law">3</a> then gives the conditional law. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-16"></a>
#### Comparison through a collar

<a id="stmt-prelim-collar"></a>
<div id="prelim:collar" class="lemma">

**Lemma 5** (Bounded densities across a collar). *Suppose two positive laws have the same graph in a collar between radii $r$ and $16r$. In this collar the graph is a full annulus, or a bounded number of sectors separated by straight coordinate walls; coincident slit banks are allowed. Their deterministic wire portions agree there. Only boundedly many wire blocks traverse the collar, and no other identifications jump it. One radial side faces an arbitrary unknown partition, whereas the graph and deterministic wires toward the other side are fixed. The marginal densities on edges beyond that other side are mutually bounded by a constant independent of scale and of the far graph. Equivalently, their expectations of every nonnegative remote function are comparable with this same constant.*

*The conclusion also holds for a fixed-shape rectangular bulk collar shielding a long box, with a constant depending on its shape.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prelim-collar"><summary>Proof of stmt-prelim-collar</summary>

*Proof.* First work on a finite graph and a finite remote edge set. Split each through wire transversally, preserving its connections on each side and retaining just one representative connection across the cut. The unknown data induce a partition $\xi$ at their section. Include all common deterministic wires for every choice of $\xi$.

For two ordered partitions, the likelihood ratio of the coarser law to the finer law is increasing: the rank of the additional identifications decreases as open components merge. Its marginal likelihood ratio on the remote set remains increasing, by the domain Markov property and conditional FKG. Consequently its maximum is attained at the all-open configuration and its minimum at the all-closed configuration. It is enough to compare those two events for the maximal and minimal partitions; every other partition lies between them.

An actual primal crosscut in every sector, or a primal circuit in the annulus, screens the remote graph with uniformly positive probability. Such screens can be discovered from the unknown side without examining edges strictly beyond them. In a sector, explore all actual dual paths from its unknown-facing arc and query edges incident to the reached dual vertices. If a primal wall-to-wall crossing exists, the search does not reach the remote arc. The elementary complementary crossing alternative then places a blocking primal path among the queried edges: otherwise, setting the unqueried primal edges closed would produce a dual crossing. The alternative follows by tracing the perimeter of the actual component reachable from the starting side; corner gap vertices belong to the arcs when their color permits. The annular version is the alternative between a primal circuit and a radial dual connection. Perform the searches in a subcollar leaving space before both sections. Reversing colors gives the dual searches as well.

Condition on a successful primal search under the minimal law. Each screen is already connected. Joining all screens and the bounded number of through-wire representatives requires only boundedly many additional block identifications. Each has an unnormalized weight ratio in $[q^{-1},1]$, hence changes expectations by a bounded density factor. The resulting partition dominates every partition transmitted from the unknown side. In particular it dominates the maximal law restricted at this same screen geometry, without requiring that law to contain the screen. The positive probability of the search proves the desired comparison of all-open probabilities.

For all-closed probabilities, make the actual dual searches under the maximal law. No actual primal path crosses these screens. Only the boundedly many through-wire representatives can still transmit ties; remove these ties at bounded cost. The resulting free cut is stochastically smaller on the remote graph than any other imposed cut partition, including the restriction of the minimal law. This proves the decreasing-event comparison. The extremal likelihood-ratio argument now gives the assertion for every remote event and every nonnegative remote function. Exhaustion proves the infinite-exterior version. For a rectangular bulk collar use the corresponding enclosing-circuit searches. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-prelim-relative-collar"></a>
<div id="prelim:relative-collar" class="lemma">

**Lemma 6** (Relative comparison). *Under the hypotheses of Lemma <a href="#prelim:collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:collar">5</a>, suppose successive collars have one of the following geometries:*

1.  *a full annulus, or one sector whose through wires are precisely continuous primal wire portions along its side rays;*

2.  *two sectors, with primal wires along both side rays of one sector and no through wires in the other, and no further fixed contacts between the sectors.*

*After $m$ further collars of a sufficiently large fixed radius ratio, the remote expectations of every fixed nonnegative function under two possible unknown-side laws have ratio $1+O((1-c)^m)$, or both expectations vanish. The conclusion holds in either radial direction, also after positive modifications or tilts supported on the unknown side.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prelim-relative-collar"><summary>Proof of stmt-prelim-relative-collar</summary>

*Proof.* Use a radius ratio such as $256$ to leave two subcollars of the preceding type. Lemma <a href="#prelim:collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:collar">5</a>, applied nearer the unknown side, gives a common marginal part of uniformly positive mass on the other subcollar. Couple those configurations identically on a fixed fraction of a reference marginal. In case (i), additionally impose a primal screen meeting and joining every through wire. In case (ii), impose a primal screen on the wired side and a dual screen on the other side. These requirements have uniformly positive conditional probability. On their occurrence the partition transmitted to the next section depends only on the shared configuration: every route through the unknown region must enter and leave through a primal screen already connected to its through wires, and the other sector transmits no primal connection.

For a nonnegative remote function, take the largest and smallest expectations over partitions at each successive section. Conditioning nests these intervals of possible expectations. The common part just constructed contracts their difference by a factor $1-c$. Their ratio is bounded initially by Lemma <a href="#prelim:collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:collar">5</a>; iterating therefore gives the stated relative estimate. A positive unknown-side tilt is a mixture over the same partitions. In particular, when propagating away from a gap, wire connections made or lost inside that gap belong to the unknown partition, which explains the need for both colors of screen in case (ii). ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-17"></a>
#### Passages and positive local tilts

Raw strands use only tile switches and stop when they reach a wall port. A passage count in a buffered annulus counts disjoint strand passages through its prescribed inner and outer rims; the outer buffer allows cropping at both rims.

<a id="stmt-prelim-passages"></a>
<div id="prelim:passages" class="lemma">

<a id="prelim:passage-moment"></a>
**Lemma 7** (Exponential passage moments). *In any fixed buffered annulus or sector of the preceding types, a raw passage count $X$ satisfies $$\label{prelim:passage-moment}
 \mathbb E[\exp(BX)\mid\text{exterior}]\le C_B
 \qquad(0\le B<\infty),$$ uniformly in scale and in exterior states inducing the specified graph and arbitrary boundary partition. The same holds for a fixed finite family of macroscopic passage counts in a fixed geometry.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prelim-passages"><summary>Proof of stmt-prelim-passages</summary>

*Proof.* First obtain one positive exponential rate. Disjoint simple radial strand subarcs split a slightly cropped annulus into ordered strips. Along each passage is an actual primal crossing path. Paths in distinct strips cannot join in the cropped graph, because open primal edges cannot cross the intervening medial separators. Choose the endpoint rim bands strictly inside the region traversed by the separators. Thus $X$ passages force at least $X/2-O(1)$ different crossing components in the actual cropped graph.

Explore complete actual components successively from one rim, ignoring all external identifications when deciding membership in a component. After a component is removed, its incident unexplored boundary edges are closed. The surviving FK law is dominated by full wiring at the original rims and walls; removing vertices can only decrease actual crossings. Even with this full wiring an actual dual blocker across the cropped annulus has probability at least $c>0$. Conditional on every successful discovery, the chance of another crossing is therefore at most $1-c$. The number of components has a geometric tail, proving <a href="#prelim:passage-moment" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="prelim:passage-moment">[prelim:passage-moment]</a> for one $B>0$.

To obtain any fixed rate, divide the radial distance into $J$ separated slices of thickness comparable to $r/J$. Cover a middle rim in each slice by $O(J)$ small boxes whose buffered annuli remain within the slice. Use wall-centered boxes near a straight wall and smaller bulk boxes elsewhere, counting the two sides of a wall separately. The overlap graph has a bounded coloring independent of $J$. Every original passage crosses one small annulus in each slice, so $$JX\le\sum_i X_i,$$ with $O(J^2)$ counts having the first exponential bound. Conditional iteration within each color class, followed by Hölder across the bounded number of colors, gives a rate $c'J$. Choose $J$ arbitrarily large but fixed. Before these boxes fit in the mesh, a deterministic finite-size bound suffices. A finite covering by bulk, straight-wall, and corner buffers gives the macroscopic version: a strand segment of the designated diameter must leave one box of an inner cover whose outer buffer is much smaller than that diameter. ◻

</details>

<a id="prelim:nest-increments"></a>
Let $N_j$ count raw nests wholly inside radius $r_j$, where the radii are dyadic and the local sector geometry extends beyond the largest radius by a buffer. A nest is a closed loop surrounding a bulk site, or an arc joining the opposite side rays around a boundary gap, corner, change, or slit tip. Then $$\label{prelim:nest-increments}
 0\le N_j-N_{j-1}\le X_j,$$ where $X_j$ is a finite family of passage counts in a band near $r_j$. Its buffer is disjoint from $B_{r_{j-k}}$ for a fixed $k$. Indeed a newly included nest either travels a fixed fraction of the radius or goes around the point within the band. At a slit tip, reaching the other bank without approaching the tip requires traversing the full-angle sector. Small-box coverings away from the center give the asserted $X_j$. Start the levels at a fixed mesh radius so the initial count is bounded.

<a id="stmt-prelim-tilts"></a>
<div id="prelim:tilts" class="lemma">

**Lemma 8** (Local tilt bounds). *For fixed $b>0$, put $$F_j=\mathbb E b^{N_j},\qquad
 d\nu_j=F_j^{-1}b^{N_j}\,d\mathbb P.$$ The ratios $F_j/F_{j-1}$ are bounded above and below uniformly. Under $\nu_j$, the shell counts $X_i$ at and beyond the outer tilt level, $i\ge j$, have all fixed exponential moments uniformly bounded. The assertions remain conditional on exterior data of the specified geometry and allow adjoining a fixed family of passage counts with buffers at or beyond that level.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prelim-tilts"><summary>Proof of stmt-prelim-tilts</summary>

*Proof.* The case $b=1$ is Lemma <a href="#prelim:passages" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:passages">7</a>. For $0<b<1$, set $D_i=\log(F_{i-1}/F_i)\ge0$. Jensen’s inequality and the exponential bound give, for any sufficiently small fixed $\varepsilon>0$, $$\begin{aligned}
 D_i
 &\le |\log b|\,\mathbb E_{\nu_{i-1}}X_i\\
 &\le\varepsilon\log
       \mathbb E_{\nu_{i-1}}
          \exp\bigl(|\log b|X_i/\varepsilon\bigr)\\
 &\le C_\varepsilon+
       \varepsilon\sum_{i-k<l<i}D_l.
\end{aligned}$$ In the last inequality, drop decreasing factors back to level $i-k$. The remaining tilt is supported outside the buffer of $X_i$, so the conditional passage bound applies. Choose $\varepsilon(k-1)<1$; induction bounds every $D_i$. Dropping the same bounded number of levels then proves every asserted exponential moment.

For $b>1$, choose $B>k\log b$ as large as desired and induct on $j$ that $\mathbb E_{\nu_j}e^{BX_i}\le C_*$ for $i\ge j$. When $i\ge j+k$, the tilt and the buffer are disjoint. Otherwise let $j_0=i-k<j$. The normalizing increment from $j_0$ to $j$ is at least one, so $$\mathbb E_{\nu_j}e^{BX_i}
 \le\mathbb E_{\nu_{j_0}}
 \exp\left(BX_i+(\log b)\sum_{j_0<l\le j}X_l\right).$$ Give each summand in the sum Hölder weight $\log b/B$ and use the inductive bound at the earlier tilt $j_0$. The remaining Hölder factor is an exponential moment of $X_i$ at a larger fixed rate, whose buffer is disjoint from the tilt at $j_0$. The right side is at most $C C_*^{k\log b/B}$, which closes the induction for sufficiently large $C_*$. Negative levels mean no tilt. The moment bounds give the ratio bounds using <a href="#prelim:nest-increments" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="prelim:nest-increments">[prelim:nest-increments]</a>. The argument is unchanged after adjoining the indicated passage counts. ◻

</details>

Consequently the expectations of these local weights and their fixed powers have logarithms of size $O(\log n)$ up to radius $O(n^C)$ in mesh units. Changing a cutoff radius by a fixed factor costs a bounded ratio. Spatially separated local tilts can be treated successively by conditioning on their disjoint patches, or by Lemma <a href="#prelim:collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:collar">5</a>. Finally, log convexity between a given power and twice that power shows that increasing the power by $\varepsilon$ costs only $n^{O(\varepsilon)}$.

<a id="stmt-prelim-absorb"></a>
<div id="prelim:absorb" class="lemma">

**Lemma 9** (Absorbing macroscopic errors). *Suppose $Y_n\ge0$, $\mathbb E Y_n\ge n^{-A}/C$, and $\mathbb E Y_n^2\le Cn^A$, whereas $X_n\ge0$ has uniformly bounded exponential moments at every fixed rate. For fixed $C_0\ge1$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, $$C_\varepsilon^{-1}n^{-\varepsilon}
 \le
 \frac{\mathbb E[Y_n C_0^{\pm X_n}]}{\mathbb E Y_n}
 \le C_\varepsilon n^{\varepsilon}.$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prelim-absorb"><summary>Proof of stmt-prelim-absorb</summary>

*Proof.* Choose $\eta>0$ so that $\eta\log C_0<\varepsilon$ and split at $X_n=\eta\log n$. On the first event the multiplicative factor lies between $n^{-\varepsilon}$ and $n^{\varepsilon}$. Cauchy–Schwarz and the exponential moment bound at an arbitrarily large fixed rate make both $\mathbb E[Y_n;X_n>\eta\log n]$ and $\mathbb E[Y_n C_0^{X_n};X_n>\eta\log n]$ smaller than any prescribed inverse power after accounting for the polynomial second moment. Choose that power larger than $A+1$. Division by the stated lower bound for $\mathbb E Y_n$ proves both estimates, enlarging constants for bounded $n$. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-18"></a>
#### Comparing slit partition functions

<a id="stmt-prelim-surface"></a>
<div id="prelim:surface" class="lemma">

<a id="prelim:surface-factorization"></a>
**Lemma 10** (Surface partition comparison). *Let finitely many straight finite wall segments have fixed macroscopic shapes and positive mutual separation. Complete each as a positive isolated boundary slit. Let $Z_s$ be its partition function relative to the unmodified plane law, and $Z_{\rm all}$ the corresponding partition function with all slits. Uniformly in the mesh, $$\label{prelim:surface-factorization}
 Z_{\rm all}\asymp\prod_s Z_s.$$ Reversing every cap-wire polarity on both banks of a straight isolated segment with boundedly many changes alters $Z_s$ by a bounded factor. The same comparison holds for a segment and its image, with transported cap data, under a symmetry of the homogeneous tile lattice, with the two color names exchanged when the symmetry exchanges the color lattices.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prelim-surface"><summary>Proof of stmt-prelim-surface</summary>

*Proof.* Enclose each segment in its own patch with a vacant bulk tile collar and room for a further disjoint buffer. Let $X_s$ be a passage count through that collar. Compare the incremental loop change $\Delta\ell_s$ of the slit surgery with $\Delta\ell_s^\circ$ computed after closing the patch ports by the same arbitrary pairing before and after the surgery. Their difference is $O(X_s)$. To see this, cut the segment ports. The background pairing is determined within the patch except for ends whose strand first traverses the collar. There are $O(X_s)$ such ends, and changing their pairing changes either completed cycle count by at most their number, also when other surgeries have been made outside.

Put $G_s=d^{\Delta\ell_s^\circ}\mathbf1_{\{X_s\le K\}}$. For fixed sufficiently large $K$, simultaneous truncation has probability bounded below under the normalized law with all completed slits, by Lemma <a href="#prelim:passages" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:passages">7</a>. On the truncated event the surgery weights and their local versions are comparable. Therefore $$Z_{\rm all}\asymp\mathbb E_0\prod_sG_s,
 \qquad Z_s\asymp\mathbb E_0G_s,$$ where $\mathbb E_0$ is the unmodified plane expectation. Apply Lemma <a href="#prelim:collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:collar">5</a> successively to the separated patch factors to obtain <a href="#prelim:surface-factorization" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="prelim:surface-factorization">[prelim:surface-factorization]</a>.

Translate an isolated segment by one tile step in its tangent direction. This is a symmetry of the homogeneous plane loop law, with duality interchanging the colors when needed. Its shifted local caps agree with the reversed caps except at boundedly many ports near tips and changes. Their remaining pairings differ on only boundedly many ends, which has bounded cycle-count cost. Applying such a lattice symmetry to the isolated slit and its cap data gives the last assertion. This is a comparison of partition functions; it does not assert bounded pointwise density for changing all pairings along a wall. ◻

</details>

<a id="sec:exponents"></a>
### Logarithmic short-distance comparisons

Only the strict range $1\le q<4$ is considered in this section. We require inequalities between logarithmic costs, not the existence of limiting critical exponents. Put <a id="exp:parameters"></a>$$\label{exp:parameters}
 \Delta=\frac{\pi}{2\lambda}-\frac32,\qquad
 s=\Delta+1,\qquad t=-\Delta,\qquad
 f(g)=\frac{\sin((2-g)\lambda)\sin((1+g)\lambda)}
                 {\sin(2\lambda)\sin\lambda}.$$ In the local experiments below, the cutoff radius is comparable to $n$ in mesh units, the specified local geometry extends beyond it by a fixed buffer, and the exterior has any fixed compatible positive completion.

<a id="pm-h-20"></a>
#### Local costs and their conventions

<a id="exp:charge-range"></a>
At a flat change of wire color, let $P(n)$ be the logarithm of the probability of an actual arm of the gap vertex’s color reaching the cutoff radius. Let $N$ count raw arcs straddling the change, from one side ray to the other, wholly inside that radius, and set $$D_*(n)=\log\mathbb E[d^N].$$ At a corner without a wire flip, write $i=0$ if the gap color agrees with the designated wire color and $i=1$ otherwise. For a convex right-angle corner and a reentrant right-angle turn respectively, define $$C_i(n)=\log\mathbb E[f(1/2)^{N/2}],\qquad
 L_i(n)=\log\mathbb E[f(-1/2)^{N/2}],$$ where again $N$ counts local straddling raw arcs. Finally, at a bulk vertex, let $N$ count closed raw nests surrounding it and set <a id="exp:bulk-weights"></a>$$\label{exp:bulk-weights}
 F_\pm(a;n)=\mathbb E[u_\pm(a)^N],\qquad
