Near a point $z\in S\cap T$, all boundary parameters approaching $z$ tend to its unique preimage under $L$. Nearby points of the approximating closed disk can therefore be connected near $z$: first go by a closest segment to the boundary, and then use the short boundary arc between the resulting nearby parameters. The closest segments stay in the closed disk. The errors are uniform along the walk; otherwise compactness would give one of the two local situations just considered and contradict failure of uniformity. The lifted closed walk still winds about $x$, whereas $x$ lies outside the approximating disk. This contradicts contractibility of that disk and proves the escape assertion.

Choose a large square $Q$ containing $\overline V$ in its interior. Take finite increasingly fine nets of $\overline E\cap Q$ whose vertices belong to $E$. Join each net vertex to an exterior collar of $Q$ using the escape assertion. The finitely many additional boundary-centered balls can have arbitrarily small total $\beta$-content. Select a finite polygonal tree joining these paths to one root on $\partial Q$, otherwise lying in the open allowed region; gridding the paths and deleting cycles gives such a tree with axis-parallel edges. Remove a sufficiently thin polygonal neighborhood of this tree, attached to $\partial Q$. Using narrow rectangular links and square junctions leaves one simple rectilinear polygon $B$. Keep an open part of the collar outside $\overline V$ in $B$.

As the nets become finer, the removed tree approaches every point of $\overline E\cap Q$. Any part of it entering $U$ lies in the protecting balls, whose radii tend to zero and whose centers lie on $T$ or $\partial V$. Hence compact subsets of $U$ persist, while the pointed kernels cannot extend through an excluded point. This proves the first two assertions.

For the finite selection, fix the tree and its closed thin neighborhood. It is compact and lies in the union of $E$ and the countable protecting balls. A finite subcover uses compact subsets of $E$ and finitely many of those balls, with a positive margin. The compact subsets of $E$ are disjoint from the closed disks bounded by $L_n$ for all large $n$. Thus only the finitely many selected balls can contain cuts affecting the discrete pockets. Their total content is no larger than that of the full cover. This is why the countable cover is used before selecting the tree. A further $O(\delta)$ adjustment makes the comparison polygon a regular wall polygon on the appropriate color lattice, without losing the protecting margins. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-108"></a>
#### Transfer of the conditional field

<a id="stmt-q4pocket-rough-transfer"></a>
<div id="q4pocket:rough-transfer" class="proposition">

**Proposition 89** (Rough-interior moment transfer). *Condition on exterior pocket data converging to a containing contour as in Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:protected-cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:protected-cuts">88</a>. At every fixed distinct tuple of points in $U$, the joint moments of the residual zero-offset height converge to the Wick moments of independent fields $\sigma\Phi^0_\Omega$ in the components $\Omega$ of $U$. This holds along every such convergent sequence of exterior data. Several containing contours at one generation may be treated simultaneously, taking the product over them.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-q4pocket-rough-transfer"><summary>Proof of stmt-q4pocket-rough-transfer</summary>

*Proof.* Write $\beta>0$ for the power in the free-bank arm bound. Fix a comparison polygon $B$ and the finite protecting balls supplied by Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:protected-cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:protected-cuts">88</a>. In every pocket delete opposite-color edges outside the lattice approximation of $B$. Equivalently, intersect its set of elementary wall-color cells with the corresponding cell set of $B$, retaining only opposite-color edges between surviving adjacent cell centers. All changes are in the protecting balls.

<a id="q4pocket:cut-error"></a>
The original opposite-color laws are product free laws. Couple them with the modified laws by exploring, in the larger law, the actual clusters incident to the deleted edges. Once those clusters are exposed, all discrepancies are shielded and the unqueried graphs have the same conditional law. The argument is the same as the gap-closing coupling in Section <a href="#sec:q4regular" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:q4regular">18</a>. If the ball radii are $r_i$ and $e>0$ is fixed, the probability that a discrepancy reaches farther than $e$ from their centers is at most $$C\sum_i(r_i/e)^\beta.
 \label{q4pocket:cut-error}$$ Indeed every such discrepancy supplies an actual opposite-color arm in the original product free law, dominated by the full-lattice comparison. Contours through changed switches have banks in these discovered clusters and obey the same locality bound. Choose $e$ smaller than the tuple’s separation and its clearance from $T\cup\partial V$. Every sign-averaged residual moment term uses a contour of at least the pair-separation diameter. The macroscopic count moments and Hölder’s inequality therefore make the moment error tend to zero with the total protecting content in <a href="#q4pocket:cut-error" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q4pocket:cut-error">[q4pocket:cut-error]</a>.

We verify the laws and offsets of the retained regions. Each side-connected component of the retained wall-color cells is again a simple polygon disk. Every globally missing cell has a path of missing cells to the exterior: it is outside at least one of the two simple grid polygons being intersected. Thus a retained component has no hole. Its boundary cannot pinch at a vertex with two opposite retained cells in that component and two opposite missing cells. The retained pair would be connected by a side-adjacent path, while the missing pair is connected through the exterior; these two disjoint connections between alternating sectors contradict planar separation. Apply this argument separately to each old pocket. The retained free opposite-color graph hence factors into independent homogeneous disk laws.

Each retained component also reaches an *old* pocket wall. Start from one of its cells and take a side-adjacent path in $B$ to the part of $B$ outside $\overline V$. The first exit from the old pocket crosses an old wall edge; the path before that exit remains in the same retained component. The component therefore has an actual wall-color connection to the old wall. No exterior contour can surround it and add an unrecorded height jump. Its residual offset is zero. Finally, a connected compact neighborhood of any test point began in one old pocket for large $n$: the bank walk tracking $L_n$ winds around that compact, so Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:discrete-pockets" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:discrete-pockets">85</a> places it in a pocket.

For the upper bound, apply Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:moment-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:moment-comparison">86</a> from the retained disks into $B$, and then apply Theorem <a href="#q4field:regular-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4field:regular-domain">81</a>. For the lower bound, make no deletions. Choose one regular polygon disk compactly inside each involved component $\Omega$, containing its test points, and compare their product laws into the original pockets. Such inner disks can exhaust each simply connected $\Omega$ in the pointed-kernel sense.

Dirichlet Green functions converge along simply connected pointed kernels. Between points whose limiting kernels are different, they tend to zero; this follows by conformal mapping convergence, or by the vanishing probability of crossing the separating bottleneck before exit. Therefore the Wick kernels of both the inner polygons and the protected outer polygons converge to those of independent Dirichlet fields in the components $\Omega$. Take the mesh limit first at fixed polygons and protectors; next improve the inner and outer approximations and let their total protecting content vanish. The two bounds coincide. Already assigned ancestor signs, or the marked path’s side constants, multiply lower-order residual moments and are restored afterwards. They do not enter the moment comparison. ◻

</details>

<a id="sec:q4identification"></a>
### Identification at the endpoint and the boundary convention

<a id="pm-h-110"></a>
#### A global conditional decomposition

Take a joint subsequential limit of the height and the distinguished path in a regular two-arc polygon. For a homogeneous initial square, take a joint limit of the height and the full contour collection, including nesting levels, parent relations, and independent fair signs. These marked geometric limits can be obtained at countably many positive-diameter cutoffs decreasing to zero, moving a cutoff when necessary to avoid atoms. At each cutoff there are only a tight number of relevant contours and ancestors. Thus finite marked relations stabilize, and a diagonal extraction retains every positive limiting contour. The signs remain conditionally independent and fair given the geometry, which was sampled without using them.

Fix a nesting level $k$ in the square. Every deterministic interior point lies almost surely in a positive winding region at that level. Indeed alternating actual circuits on successively separated bulk scales force arbitrarily many surrounding contours. The domain Markov bounds and bulk RSW make the failure probability tend to zero as the number of scales grows, with the mesh limit taken first at each finite selection of scales. The same statement holds for Lebesgue-almost every point by Fubini. Winding regions of different contours at a fixed level are disjoint, as their discrete predecessors are. Positive coincident traversal arcs would also contradict the multiple-visit dimension bound. In the marked case the two side closures likewise cover almost every point away from their traces.

Let $\mathcal F_k$ denote the limiting exterior geometry and signs through level $k$, or let $\mathcal F$ denote the limiting marked path in the two-arc experiment. Let $\mathcal O$ be the collection of components of the corresponding open winding regions. Define $v$ on each component to be the sum of its containing signs through level $k$, or its marked side value $0$ or $1$. Its value on the remaining area-zero set is immaterial.

<a id="stmt-q4pocket-conditional-field"></a>
<div id="q4pocket:conditional-field" class="proposition">

<a id="q4pocket:conditional-decomposition"></a>
**Proposition 90** (Conditional field in all complementary components). *Conditional on the stated limiting exterior data, the height has the distributional decomposition $$h\ \stackrel{\mathrm{law}}=\
 v+\sigma\sum_{\Omega\in\mathcal O}\Phi^0_\Omega,
 \label{q4pocket:conditional-decomposition}$$ where the Dirichlet fields are independent and extended by zero. The identity holds as an identity of distributions on the whole initial-domain interior, not merely after restriction to individual components.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-q4pocket-conditional-field"><summary>Proof of stmt-q4pocket-conditional-field</summary>

*Proof.* For a test function $f$, the independent sum on the right exists in $L^2$, since Green-function monotonicity gives <a id="q4pocket:covariance-domination"></a>$$\sum_{\Omega\in\mathcal O}
 \iint_{\Omega^2}|f(z)|G_\Omega(z,w)|f(w)|\,dz\,dw
 \leq
 \iint_{V^2}|f(z)|G_V(z,w)|f(w)|\,dz\,dw.
 \label{q4pocket:covariance-domination}$$ The same estimate, with a fixed negative Sobolev norm, defines the sum as a random distribution.

Use a representation on which the extracted geometric data converge. A fixed distinct tuple of deterministic interior points is almost surely eventually covered, with positive limiting clearance, by the relevant winding components. Its offsets converge. Conditional on the discrete exterior pocket data, including the actual cycle walls, its residual moments converge by Proposition <a href="#q4pocket:rough-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:rough-transfer">89</a>. That proposition applies along every realized convergent data sequence; it requires no regularity of the unexplored cycle walls beyond the proved pocket properties.

To pass to conditioning only on the stated limiting data, multiply the discrete moment identities by a bounded continuous function of those data. The necessary uniform integrability follows from Lemma <a href="#q4field:moment-kernels" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4field:moment-kernels">80</a>. At level $k$, terms already assigned to ancestors have offsets bounded by $k$. The remaining sign-averaged terms require shared contours of at least the relevant pair-separation diameter, and their counts have all polynomial moments under the initial law. The marked offset is bounded by one. Thus, for each $m$, a bound of the form $$C_{m,k}\bigl(1+|\log d_*|\bigr)^m,
 \qquad
 d_* = \min\bigl\{1,|z_i-z_j|:i\ne j\bigr\},$$ and its higher-moment versions apply also before coverage by the limiting components has stabilized. Such bounds are integrable on tuples in compact subsets of $V$, including near diagonals.

Smear the identities against tensor products of smooth test densities. Fubini and uniform integrability pass every joint moment to the limit, with every bounded continuous geometric multiplier retained. The almost-everywhere coverage removes the remaining set from these integrals. Higher even moments give uniform integrability of the smeared variables themselves. A countable determining family of test densities then yields the conditional moment identities for distributions. For each fixed conditional geometry, the Gaussian law with the bounded offset on the right of <a href="#q4pocket:conditional-decomposition" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q4pocket:conditional-decomposition">[q4pocket:conditional-decomposition]</a> is moment determining; equivalently, apply the one-dimensional Gaussian moment criterion to every rational linear combination of finitely many tests. Hence the moment identities identify the conditional law. Because the tests range over the entire initial domain, this argument also excludes a residual distribution supported on the area-zero complement of the components. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-111"></a>
#### Local-set uniqueness with the exact height normalization

We use two continuum identifications. For the zero-boundary GFF, the two-valued bounded-type thin local set with values $-a,b$ is unique and field measurable when $a,b>0$ and $a+b\geq2\lambda_0$. At $a=b=2\lambda_0$ it is the non-nested $\mathrm{CLE}_4$ gasket, with independent fair labels on its holes (Aru, Sepúlveda, and Werner 2019, Propositions 1 and 2 and Sections 4 and 6.3) <a id="pm-cite-61"></a>[[AruSepulvedaWerner2019](#ref-AruSepulvedaWerner2019)].

For boundary data we use Theorem 3.21 of Aru, Lupu, and Sepúlveda (2020) <a id="pm-cite-62"></a>[[AruLupuSepulveda2020](#ref-AruLupuSepulveda2020)], with its immediately preceding boundary criterion. In the specialization needed here, the initial domain is a disk, $u$ is bounded harmonic with finitely piecewise constant boundary data in $[-a,b]$, and $a+b\geq2\lambda_0$. Uniqueness holds for bounded-type thin local sets whose total conditional harmonic function is constantly $-a$ or $b$ on each connected boundary component of each complementary domain. The interval here is closed: boundary values equal to $-a$ or $b$ are permitted. The standard completed chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_4$ level line, for boundary data $-\lambda_0,\lambda_0$ on the two arcs, has exactly this conditional field decomposition (Schramm and Sheffield 2013) <a id="pm-cite-63"></a>[[SchrammSheffield2013](#ref-SchrammSheffield2013)].

<a id="stmt-q4pocket-local-set"></a>
<div id="q4pocket:local-set" class="lemma">

**Lemma 91** (The limiting sets are bounded-type thin local sets). *For the first contour level in the square, let $$A=\overline V\setminus\bigcup_{\Omega\in\mathcal O}\Omega.$$ In the marked experiment let $A$ be the path trace together with $\partial V$. After the normalizations below, these are bounded-type thin local sets. In the homogeneous case their harmonic values are $\pm2\lambda_0$. In the marked case their *total* harmonic values are $\pm\lambda_0$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-q4pocket-local-set"><summary>Proof of stmt-q4pocket-local-set</summary>

*Proof.* In the homogeneous case, write $\Phi=h/\sigma$ and $m=v/\sigma$. Theorem <a href="#q4field:regular-domain" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4field:regular-domain">81</a> says that $\Phi$ is a zero-boundary GFF. At the first level $v\in\{-1,1\}$, so $m\in\{-2\lambda_0,2\lambda_0\}$. In the marked case put $$X=\frac{h-1/2}{\sigma}=\Phi+u,
 \qquad
 m=\frac{v-1/2}{\sigma}-u,$$ where $\Phi$ is a zero-boundary GFF and $u$ is the bounded harmonic function with boundary data $-\lambda_0,\lambda_0$ on the respective arcs. Here $|m|\leq2\lambda_0$ and $m+u\in\{-\lambda_0,\lambda_0\}$ on each component.

In either case Proposition <a href="#q4pocket:conditional-field" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:conditional-field">90</a> gives the full conditional Dirichlet law of $\Phi-m$ in $V\setminus A$. This law depends on the exterior data only through $A$. Conditioning down to $(A,m)$ proves locality. Moreover $m$ is an ordinary bounded function, integrated over $V\setminus A$, and the distributional identity has no additional part supported on $A$. This is thinness. The uniqueness of a local set’s harmonic distribution from the field and set is also part of the local-set formalism (Aru, Lupu, and Sepúlveda 2020, Lemma 2.3(1)) <a id="pm-cite-64"></a>[[AruLupuSepulveda2020](#ref-AruLupuSepulveda2020)]; no extra choice of component labels is being added at this step.

For completeness, $A$ is connected and contains the entire Jordan boundary. Its complementary components are simply connected by Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:protected-cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:protected-cuts">88</a>. If $A$ were disconnected, split it into two nonempty disjoint compact sets, putting the connected $\partial V$ in the first. A fine polygonal boundary around part of the second, at positive distance from the first and from $\partial V$, would be a closed walk in a component of $V\setminus A$ with nonzero winding about a point of $A$. This contradicts that component’s simple connectivity. Thus $A$ is a nontrivial connected compact set. It has no isolated points, and no component disjoint from $\partial V$. These facts verify the topological condition in the definition of a bounded-type thin local set. Conformal transport to a disk preserves all these assertions. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-q4pocket-regular-chordal"></a>
<div id="q4pocket:regular-chordal" class="proposition">

**Proposition 92** (Regular marked endpoint). *The distinguished curves in the regular two-arc experiments converge as ordered curves, up to increasing changes of parametrization, to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_4$ between the prescribed marks.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-q4pocket-regular-chordal"><summary>Proof of stmt-q4pocket-regular-chordal</summary>

*Proof.* Apply the boundary-data uniqueness theorem with $a=b=\lambda_0$. The initial domain, after conformal transport, has one complementary component, which is not a singleton. The boundary function has two changes and takes values in the closed allowed interval. Its interior range meets $(-\lambda_0,\lambda_0)$ by the strong maximum principle. The height-gap condition holds with equality. In every component of $V\setminus A$, the total conditional mean is constant $-\lambda_0$ or $\lambda_0$, so the stated boundary criterion holds on every boundary component. Finally Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:local-set" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:local-set">91</a> supplies thinness, boundedness, and the required topology. All hypotheses of Aru, Lupu, and Sepúlveda (2020, Theorem 3.21) <a id="pm-cite-65"></a>[[AruLupuSepulveda2020](#ref-AruLupuSepulveda2020)] are therefore met.

The completed Schramm–Sheffield level line coupled to the same field satisfies these same conditions. Uniqueness identifies the limiting closed set, together with its harmonic labels, with that level line plus the original boundary. In particular its interior trace is the simple chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_4$ arc, which has no hits on the interiors of the two boundary arcs.

This closed-set statement identifies the original ordered curve as well. Any extra boundary point off the identified compact arc has a neighborhood disjoint from that arc; reaching it would force a nonconstant boundary subtraversal, excluded by Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:geometry" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:geometry">87</a>. On a simple arc, any genuine backtracking repeats a nondegenerate subarc. Such a subarc has positive Hausdorff dimension, contradicting the dimension-zero multiple-visit bound. After suppressing constant pauses, the curve therefore traverses the arc once, in the prescribed endpoint order. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-112"></a>
#### Contours, labels, and all nesting levels

<a id="stmt-q4pocket-square-cle"></a>
<div id="q4pocket:square-cle" class="proposition">

**Proposition 93** (Endpoint contours in a square). *In a homogeneous square, the entire signed contour hierarchy converges to nested $\mathrm{CLE}_4$, with independent fair signs at each generation. The identification includes each individual contour as a simple-loop element, its parent, and its traversal order up to the loop convention.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-q4pocket-square-cle"><summary>Proof of stmt-q4pocket-square-cle</summary>

*Proof.* The first-level set $A$ in Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:local-set" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:local-set">91</a> has harmonic values $\pm2\lambda_0$. Ordinary two-valued-set uniqueness identifies its coupling with the field as the labelled non-nested $\mathrm{CLE}_4$ gasket.

<a id="q4pocket:label-grouping"></a>
We must still identify the discrete contour elements, since one such element could a priori have several winding components. Every positive contour has an interior-status disk, by the two-status property and the exclusion of boundary-only traversal. Thus it winds at least one hole of the identified gasket. Select two distinct holes by the first points they contain in a fixed countable dense set. Conditional on the gasket $A$, the two unit offsets in our construction satisfy $$\mathbb E[v(\Omega_1)v(\Omega_2)\mid A]
 =\mathbb P\{\Omega_1\text{ and }\Omega_2
        \text{ belong to one contour}\mid A\}.
 \label{q4pocket:label-grouping}$$ Indeed the signs were independent and fair given the entire unlabelled contour geometry; different contours contribute zero covariance, whereas the same contour contributes one. In the unique two-valued-set coupling, different $\mathrm{CLE}_4$ holes have independent fair labels, so the left side of <a href="#q4pocket:label-grouping" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q4pocket:label-grouping">[q4pocket:label-grouping]</a> is zero. Countability excludes all grouping of distinct holes.

Consequently each positive contour winds exactly one simple CLE hole. Its full interior trace equals that hole’s Jordan boundary: the two-status property puts every trace point on the boundary of its winding region, and winding stability puts that boundary in the trace. Additional boundary pieces are excluded as in Proposition <a href="#q4pocket:regular-chordal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:regular-chordal">92</a>. The limiting winding is one. Any extra covering or backtracking repeats a nondegenerate subarc and violates the dimension-zero bound. Thus the original contour is exactly the corresponding simple-loop element, not just a set with the same filled interior.

Proceed conditionally through the hierarchy. Given the geometry and labels through an identified level, the residual fields in its holes are independent zero-boundary GFFs by Proposition <a href="#q4pocket:conditional-field" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:conditional-field">90</a>. The next-level decomposition, with the parent constant subtracted, makes its missing set in each hole a thin local set with harmonic values $\pm2\lambda_0$. Child winding components lie in the parent by discrete winding stability at points with clearance. They are simply connected and cover almost every point, by the arguments already given. Every positive child has an interior-status disk and is supported on the closure of its winding regions by the two-status property. Thus the same topology and thinness verification applies inside each parent hole.

Conditional uniqueness, including measurability from the respective residual field, gives independent fresh CLEs in the parent holes. Equation <a href="#q4pocket:label-grouping" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q4pocket:label-grouping">[q4pocket:label-grouping]</a> and the trace argument again identify every individual child and its sign. Its parent can be read at any interior disk point off the traces. Induction identifies all finite generations. Finally every positive-diameter contour and all its ancestors occur in the retained finite-cutoff hierarchies, whose counts are tight. Sending the cutoff to zero identifies the full collection in the stated matching topology. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-q4pocket-whole-plane"></a>
<div id="q4pocket:whole-plane" class="corollary">

**Corollary 94** (Endpoint whole-plane ensemble). *The infinite-volume free critical FK loop ensemble at $q=4$ converges to the nested whole-plane $\mathrm{CLE}_4$ ensemble, in the spherical matching metric for all loops.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-q4pocket-whole-plane"><summary>Proof of stmt-q4pocket-whole-plane</summary>

*Proof.* Use the expanding-square coupling of Section <a href="#sec:loops" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:loops">15</a>. Its endpoint ingredients are bulk estimates: monotone boundary coupling and exploration of actual boundary connections couple the infinite-volume free switches with the square switches deep inside a large square, except when a boundary connection reaches the inner region. Actual dual circuits on successive annuli block that event, uniformly even under the maximal boundary law. Actual-color annular blockers likewise make a loop from a fixed disk reaching the coupling boundary unlikely. The finite-square limit is given by Proposition <a href="#q4pocket:square-cle" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:square-cle">93</a>.

Nested simple CLEs in domains of conformal radius tending to infinity converge locally to nested whole-plane CLE; their spherical whole-plane law is Möbius invariant (Kemppainen and Werner 2016, Theorem 1, Proposition 4, and Section 3.2) <a id="pm-cite-66"></a>[[KemppainenWerner2016](#ref-KemppainenWerner2016)]. Its range $8/3<\kappa\leq4$ includes the present endpoint, and centered expanding squares meet its conformal-radius condition.

To pass from the local comparison to the spherical metric, first fix a spherical diameter cutoff. Loops lying entirely outside a sufficiently large fixed disk are below that cutoff. With high probability, every other loop above the cutoff remains inside the switch-coupling region, by the preceding escape bound. The number of such loops is tight, and the finite-square matching identifies them bijectively with their traversal order. Take the mesh limit, then enlarge the square and the fixed disk, and finally send the diameter cutoff to zero. This is the required global matching statement, including all nesting levels. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-113"></a>
#### The prescribed marked Jordan approximations

It remains to transfer Proposition <a href="#q4pocket:regular-chordal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:regular-chordal">92</a> to the precise wired/free edge convention of the theorem. This transfer uses actual color walls, so that a boundary identification is never mistaken for a path in the lattice.

<a id="stmt-q4pocket-jordan-chordal"></a>
<div id="q4pocket:jordan-chordal" class="proposition">

**Proposition 95** (Endpoint marked Jordan convergence). *For every marked uniform Jordan approximation specified in the theorem, its critical $q=4$ distinguished curve converges to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_4$ in the limiting marked domain.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-q4pocket-jordan-chordal"><summary>Proof of stmt-q4pocket-jordan-chordal</summary>

*Proof.* Use the two-change disk drawing from Lemma <a href="#moving:drawing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="moving:drawing">35</a>: place tiles on every polygon-graph edge, give boundary edges distinct exterior tabs, and put local caps along the wired primal and complementary dual arcs. Flattening the tabs and separating the drawing in a thin collar changes the ordered curve by only $O(\delta_n)$ in uniform distance. Boundary edges on the wired primal arc may be fixed open, while edges on the free arc retain their sampled law.

The primal bank of the distinguished path, closed along the primal wall, is a walk of actual open edges in the wired cluster. On the other side, the actual internal dual bank, its exits to exterior copies across the free arc, and the local complementary-wire links give the dual closing walk. All artificial dual links and copies stay within $O(\delta_n)$ of that free arc. No dual exit through the primal wired arc is used. At fixed bulk points away from limiting traces these walks therefore have stable complementary winding statuses $1$ and $0$. Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:geometry" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:geometry">87</a> gives tightness, the two-status property, and the restrictions on multiple visits and boundary traversal for these drawings.

Construct a regular comparison polygon $V^+$ close to the limiting marked domain $V$ with the following two strict separations: the original primal wired arc, including its endpoints, lies outside $\overline{V^+}$; and the comparison dual wall lies outside $\overline V$. All margins are fixed before taking the mesh limit. One construction uses plane Schoenflies coordinates for $\partial V$. Move the primal portion slightly inward, extending it a little beyond both marks, then rise outside the unit circle near the two ends and put both comparison transitions there. Keep the whole comparison dual portion outside the unit circle. Approximate the resulting simple curve by a simple rectilinear polygon, preserving all strict margins, and place the transitions inside straight sides. Its actual primal-open and dual-open wall approximations are regular experiments. Reverse the colors to construct $V^-$: the original complementary arc is outside $\overline{V^-}$, and the comparison primal wall is outside $\overline V$. Both comparisons approach the same marked Jordan domain as the offsets vanish.

Couple the original law with that in $V^+$ so that every original primal open edge in the common region is open in the comparison. To check the boundary partition needed for this ordering, restrict the original configuration to the common edges. Any connection departing from the comparison disk can induce ties only at its actual primal wall vertices: its dual wall and transitions lie outside the entire original closure, while the original wired vertices lie outside the comparison. The comparison connects all those primal wall vertices by fixed open wall edges. Its induced partition therefore dominates the original one, and random-cluster monotonicity gives the coupling. The cut is along a primal lattice wall, so no unaligned edge crossing is being treated as a wall vertex.

Every piece inside $V^+$ of the original primal closing bank walk belongs to the comparison primal wall cluster: follow its original connection to the outer wire and take its first exit from $V^+$. Suppose a test point has original primal winding status but comparison dual status, with positive clearance. On the comparison dual side it can be joined to the comparison dual wall without crossing the comparison primal wall cluster, and hence without crossing the original closing walk inside $V^+$. From that wall, which is outside the entire original polygon, it can escape to infinity through the original exterior. This contradicts the original winding. Thus original primal status implies comparison primal status.

For $V^-$ apply exactly the dual ordering. Original dual identifications and artificial bank links lie beside the complementary arc, outside $V^-$. In the common region the dual walk uses only internal dual steps, and departing connections induce ties only at the aligned comparison dual wall vertices. An originally wired primal edge admits no dual crossing step. Original dual status therefore implies comparison dual status. The free-bank arm bound removes near-hits and tile ambiguities at any prescribed finite tuple of bulk points.

<a id="q4pocket:side-sandwich"></a>
Let $I_n(z)$ be the original primal-side indicator, and let $I_n^-(z),I_n^+(z)$ denote those in the two comparisons. The separate monotone couplings give, for every fixed finite tuple $\boldsymbol z$, the stochastic bounds $$(I_n^-(z))_{z\in\boldsymbol z}
 \ \preceq\
 (I_n(z))_{z\in\boldsymbol z}
 \ \preceq\
 (I_n^+(z))_{z\in\boldsymbol z},
 \label{q4pocket:side-sandwich}$$ up to errors vanishing with the mesh. At fixed comparison polygons the limiting laws are the regular chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_4$ laws by Proposition <a href="#q4pocket:regular-chordal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:regular-chordal">92</a>. Now let the offsets vanish. Conformal maps and their boundary extensions converge under marked uniform Jordan convergence, using uniform local connectivity of these boundary parametrizations. The two comparison SLE laws therefore have the same limit. Deterministic interior points avoid SLE, so their side-status arrays converge as well. Equation <a href="#q4pocket:side-sandwich" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q4pocket:side-sandwich">[q4pocket:side-sandwich]</a> identifies every finite-dimensional status law of an original subsequential limit.

On a fixed countable dense set, the statuses determine the interior trace: an interior trace point has both statuses in every neighborhood, whereas a point off the trace has a small disk of constant status. This follows from Lemma <a href="#q4pocket:geometry" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:geometry">87</a>. Thus the limiting interior trace is the SLE trace. No boundary traversal and the dimension-zero multiple-visit bound identify the complete ordered curve exactly as in Proposition <a href="#q4pocket:regular-chordal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4pocket:regular-chordal">92</a>. Every tight subsequence has the same law, proving the full-sequence assertion. ◻

</details>
